text_es: Create a query `valuations` that identifies bookshops holding highly valuable rare books. The database includes tables for bookshops, book inventory, and expert appraisals. Join the tables to calculate the total appraised value of first edition books at each shop. Filter the dataset to include only hardcover books and appraisals completed this year. Group the records by the shop name and the city it operates in. Show only the shops whose total rare book value is greater than ten thousand dollars. Sort the results alphabetically by the city.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE bookshops (
    shop_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    shop_name    VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    city         VARCHAR(80)  NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE books (
    book_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    shop_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES bookshops (shop_id),
    title        VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    edition      VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    binding      VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE appraisals (
    appraisal_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    book_id          INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES books (book_id),
    appraiser        VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    appraised_value  NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL,
    appraisal_date   DATE NOT NULL,
    status           VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW rare_hardcover_books AS
SELECT
    b.book_id,
    b.shop_id,
    b.title
FROM
    books AS b
WHERE
    b.binding = 'hardcover'
    AND b.edition = 'first';

CREATE VIEW appraisals_this_year AS
SELECT
    a.book_id,
    a.appraised_value
FROM
    appraisals AS a
WHERE
    a.status = 'completed'
    AND
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM a.appraisal_date)
            = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE);

CREATE VIEW valuations AS
SELECT
    s.shop_name,
    s.city,
    COUNT(*) AS rare_book_count,
    SUM(v.appraised_value) AS total_rare_value
FROM
    bookshops AS s
    JOIN
        rare_hardcover_books AS r
        ON r.shop_id = s.shop_id
    JOIN
        appraisals_this_year AS v
        ON v.book_id = r.book_id
GROUP BY
    s.shop_name,
    s.city
HAVING
    SUM(v.appraised_value) > 10000
ORDER BY
    s.city;

CREATE VIEW city_valuation_summary AS
SELECT
    v.city,
    COUNT(*) AS qualifying_shops,
    SUM(v.total_rare_value) AS city_total_value
FROM
    valuations AS v
GROUP BY
    v.city;

SELECT
    v.city,
    v.shop_name,
    v.rare_book_count,
    v.total_rare_value,
    ROUND(100.0 * v.total_rare_value / c.city_total_value, 1) AS pct_of_city_value
FROM
    valuations AS v
    JOIN
        city_valuation_summary AS c
        ON c.city = v.city
ORDER BY
    v.city,
    v.total_rare_value DESC;

text_es: Write a view `finalists` that selects the top performing choirs in a regional music festival. Use tables for choirs, choir members, and performance scores. Connect the data to find the average harmony score for each choir. Filter the entries to include only adult choirs and performances in the classical category. Group the information by the choir name and their conductor. Retain only the choirs that scored above ninety points on average. Order the final output by the score descending.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE choirs (
    choir_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    choir_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    conductor VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    age_category VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE choir_members (
    member_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    choir_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES choirs (choir_id),
    member_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    voice_part VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE performance_scores (
    score_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    member_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES choir_members (member_id),
    category VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
    harmony_score NUMERIC(5, 2) NOT NULL,
    performance_date DATE NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW finalists AS
SELECT c.choir_name,
       c.conductor,
       AVG(p.harmony_score) AS average_harmony
FROM choirs
    AS c
JOIN choir_members
    AS m
    ON m.choir_id = c.choir_id
JOIN performance_scores
    AS p
    ON p.member_id = m.member_id
WHERE c.age_category = 'adult'
    AND p.category = 'classical'
GROUP BY c.choir_name,
         c.conductor
HAVING AVG(p.harmony_score) > 90
ORDER BY average_harmony DESC;

SELECT choir_name,
       conductor,
       ROUND(average_harmony, 1) AS final_score
FROM finalists
ORDER BY average_harmony DESC;

SELECT f.choir_name,
       m.voice_part,
       COUNT(*) AS singers
FROM finalists
    AS f
JOIN choirs
    AS c
    ON c.choir_name = f.choir_name
    AND c.conductor = f.conductor
JOIN choir_members
    AS m
    ON m.choir_id = c.choir_id
GROUP BY f.choir_name,
         m.voice_part
ORDER BY f.choir_name,
         singers DESC;

SELECT f.choir_name,
       f.conductor,
       MAX(p.harmony_score) AS best_single_score,
       MAX(p.performance_date) AS latest_performance
FROM finalists
    AS f
JOIN choirs
    AS c
    ON c.choir_name = f.choir_name
    AND c.conductor = f.conductor
JOIN choir_members
    AS m
    ON m.choir_id = c.choir_id
JOIN performance_scores
    AS p
    ON p.member_id = m.member_id
WHERE p.category = 'classical'
GROUP BY f.choir_name,
         f.conductor
ORDER BY best_single_score DESC;

from finalists

text_es: Write a query `yields` that calculates the most productive community gardens. The system has tables for gardens, individual plots, and harvest records. Link these tables to sum the total pounds of vegetables harvested. Filter the records to only include summer harvests and plots managed by community groups. Group the data by the garden name and the neighborhood. Include only gardens that produced over two thousand pounds of food. Order the results by the total harvest weight in descending order.
text_nat:
-- Community garden productivity module: schema, reporting views and a driver.

CREATE TABLE gardens (
    garden_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    garden_name   TEXT    NOT NULL,
    neighborhood  TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE plots (
    plot_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    garden_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES gardens (garden_id),
    plot_label    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    manager_type  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    size_sqft     INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE harvests (
    harvest_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    plot_id          INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES plots (plot_id),
    harvest_date     DATE    NOT NULL,
    season           TEXT    NOT NULL,
    crop             TEXT    NOT NULL,
    pounds_harvested NUMERIC NOT NULL
);

-- Base view: only summer harvests taken from community-group plots.
CREATE VIEW summer_community_harvests
AS
SELECT
    h.harvest_id,
    p.garden_id,
    h.crop,
    h.pounds_harvested
FROM harvests
    AS h
JOIN plots
    AS p
    ON p.plot_id = h.plot_id
WHERE h.season = 'Summer'
    AND p.manager_type = 'community group';

-- Most productive gardens: over 2000 lb of summer food from community plots.
CREATE VIEW yields
AS
SELECT
    g.garden_name,
    g.neighborhood,
    SUM(s.pounds_harvested) AS total_pounds
FROM summer_community_harvests
    AS s
JOIN gardens
    AS g
    ON g.garden_id = s.garden_id
GROUP BY
    g.garden_name,
    g.neighborhood
HAVING SUM(s.pounds_harvested) > 2000
ORDER BY total_pounds DESC;

-- Crop breakdown restricted to the gardens that cleared the 2000 lb bar.
CREATE VIEW crop_mix
AS
SELECT
    g.neighborhood,
    s.crop,
    SUM(s.pounds_harvested) AS crop_pounds
FROM summer_community_harvests
    AS s
JOIN gardens
    AS g
    ON g.garden_id = s.garden_id
JOIN yields
    AS y
    ON y.garden_name = g.garden_name
    AND y.neighborhood = g.neighborhood
GROUP BY
    g.neighborhood,
    s.crop;

-- Driver: the ranking itself, then the crops that drove it.
SELECT
    garden_name,
    neighborhood,
    total_pounds
FROM yields
ORDER BY total_pounds DESC;

SELECT
    neighborhood,
    crop,
    crop_pounds
FROM crop_mix
WHERE crop_pounds >= 100
ORDER BY crop_pounds DESC;

text_es: Create a view `popularity` that finds the most successful pottery instructors. You have tables for studios, instructors, and class enrollments. Join the tables to determine the total number of students taught by each instructor. Filter the data to include only wheel throwing classes and instructors with more than five years of experience. Group the findings by the instructor name and the studio they work at. Keep only those instructors who have taught over two hundred students. Sort the output by the total student count descending.
text_nat:
-- Pottery studio network: schema, the `popularity` view, and reporting queries.

CREATE TABLE studios (
    studio_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    studio_name      VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    city             VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE instructors (
    instructor_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    instructor_name  VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    studio_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES studios (studio_id),
    years_experience INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE class_enrollments (
    enrollment_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    instructor_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES instructors (instructor_id),
    student_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    class_type       VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    enrolled_on      DATE NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW popularity AS
SELECT
    i.instructor_name,
    s.studio_id,
    s.studio_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.student_id) AS total_students
FROM class_enrollments
    AS e
JOIN instructors
    AS i
    ON e.instructor_id = i.instructor_id
JOIN studios
    AS s
    ON i.studio_id = s.studio_id
WHERE e.class_type = 'wheel throwing'
  AND i.years_experience > 5
GROUP BY
    i.instructor_name,
    s.studio_id,
    s.studio_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.student_id) > 200
ORDER BY total_students DESC;

-- Leaderboard handed to the marketing team.
SELECT
    p.instructor_name AS instructor,
    p.studio_name AS studio,
    p.total_students
FROM popularity
    AS p
ORDER BY p.total_students DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- How each city benefits from its top wheel-throwing teachers.
SELECT
    s.city,
    p.studio_name AS studio,
    COUNT(*) AS star_instructors,
    SUM(p.total_students) AS students_reached
FROM popularity
    AS p
JOIN studios
    AS s
    ON p.studio_id = s.studio_id
GROUP BY
    s.city,
    p.studio_name
ORDER BY students_reached DESC;

text_es: Write a procedure `winners()` that identifies the classic car clubs with the most award winning vehicles. The database contains tables for car clubs, registered vehicles, and show awards. Connect these tables to count the total number of gold ribbons won by each club. Limit the data to vehicles manufactured before nineteen seventy and awards from national level shows. Group the results by the club name and the state they are based in. Show only clubs that have won at least ten gold ribbons. Order the list alphabetically by the club name.
text_nat:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS show_awards;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS vehicles;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS car_clubs;

CREATE TABLE car_clubs (
    club_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    club_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    state     CHAR(2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE vehicles (
    vehicle_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    club_id    INT NOT NULL REFERENCES car_clubs (club_id),
    make       VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    model      VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    model_year SMALLINT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE show_awards (
    award_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicles (vehicle_id),
    show_level VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    ribbon     VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    show_year  SMALLINT NOT NULL
);

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE winners()
BEGIN
    SELECT c.club_name,
           c.state,
           COUNT(*) AS gold_ribbons
    FROM car_clubs c
    JOIN vehicles v
        ON v.club_id = c.club_id
    JOIN show_awards a
        ON a.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
    WHERE v.model_year < 1970
      AND a.show_level = 'National'
      AND a.ribbon = 'Gold'
    GROUP BY c.club_name,
             c.state
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
    ORDER BY c.club_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE club_award_detail(IN p_club_name VARCHAR(80))
BEGIN
    SELECT v.make,
           v.model,
           v.model_year,
           MIN(a.show_year) AS first_win,
           COUNT(*) AS gold_ribbons
    FROM vehicles v
    JOIN car_clubs c
        ON c.club_id = v.club_id
    JOIN show_awards a
        ON a.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
    WHERE c.club_name = p_club_name
      AND v.model_year < 1970
      AND a.show_level = 'National'
      AND a.ribbon = 'Gold'
    GROUP BY v.make,
             v.model,
             v.model_year
    ORDER BY gold_ribbons DESC,
             v.make;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL winners();
CALL club_award_detail('Bay State Cruisers');

text_es: Create a query `standings` that lists the top performing chess clubs in a statewide league. Use tables for regions, chess clubs, and match results. Join them to calculate the total number of matches won by each club. Filter the records to include only standard time control matches and clubs that have active memberships. Group the output by the club name and their region. Retain only the clubs that have won more than fifty matches this season. Sort the final standings by the number of wins from highest to lowest.
text_nat:
-- Statewide chess league: schema, standings query and season report.

CREATE TABLE regions (
    region_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    region_name TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE chess_clubs (
    club_id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    club_name         TEXT NOT NULL,
    region_id         INTEGER REFERENCES regions (region_id),
    membership_status TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE match_results (
    match_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    club_id           INTEGER REFERENCES chess_clubs (club_id),
    opponent_club_id  INTEGER REFERENCES chess_clubs (club_id),
    time_control      TEXT NOT NULL,
    result            TEXT NOT NULL,
    season            TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- Top performing clubs: wins in standard time control by active clubs.
CREATE VIEW standings AS
SELECT
      c.club_name
    , r.region_name
    , COUNT(*) AS wins
FROM match_results m
JOIN chess_clubs c
    ON m.club_id = c.club_id
JOIN regions r
    ON c.region_id = r.region_id
WHERE m.time_control = 'standard'
  AND m.result = 'win'
  AND c.membership_status = 'active'
  AND m.season = '2025'
GROUP BY
      c.club_name
    , r.region_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 50
ORDER BY wins DESC;

-- Played/won counts per club, used to derive win percentages.
CREATE VIEW club_win_rates AS
SELECT
      c.club_name
    , COUNT(*) AS matches_played
    , SUM(CASE WHEN m.result = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wins
FROM chess_clubs c
JOIN match_results m
    ON c.club_id = m.club_id
WHERE m.time_control = 'standard'
  AND m.season = '2025'
GROUP BY c.club_name;

-- Regional roll-up over the qualified clubs.
CREATE VIEW region_totals AS
SELECT
      region_name
    , COUNT(*) AS qualified_clubs
    , SUM(wins) AS region_wins
FROM standings
GROUP BY region_name;

-- Season report: standings enriched with form and regional share.
SELECT
      s.region_name
    , s.club_name
    , s.wins
    , ROUND(100.0 * w.wins / w.matches_played, 1) AS win_pct
    , ROUND(100.0 * s.wins / t.region_wins, 1) AS share_of_region
FROM standings s
JOIN club_win_rates w
    ON s.club_name = w.club_name
JOIN region_totals t
    ON s.region_name = t.region_name
ORDER BY
      s.wins DESC
    , s.region_name;

text_es: Write a view `selections` that highlights universities producing successful short films. You are given tables for universities, student directors, and festival submissions. Link the tables to count the total number of awards won by films from each university. Restrict the data to documentary films and directors in their senior year. Group the information by the university name and the country it is located in. Only include universities with more than three documentary awards. Order the results by the award count descending.
text_nat:
-- Short-film festival analytics: schema, the `selections` view, and reporting queries.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS selections;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS festival_submissions;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS student_directors;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS universities;

CREATE TABLE universities (
    university_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    university_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    country         VARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE student_directors (
    director_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    university_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES universities (university_id),
    director_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    study_year    VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE festival_submissions (
    submission_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    director_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES student_directors (director_id),
    film_title    VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL,
    genre         VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    festival_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    awards_won    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE VIEW selections AS
SELECT universities.university_name,
       universities.country,
       SUM(festival_submissions.awards_won) AS documentary_awards
FROM universities
JOIN student_directors
    ON student_directors.university_id = universities.university_id
JOIN festival_submissions
    ON festival_submissions.director_id = student_directors.director_id
WHERE festival_submissions.genre = 'Documentary'
  AND student_directors.study_year = 'Senior'
GROUP BY universities.university_name,
         universities.country
HAVING SUM(festival_submissions.awards_won) > 3
ORDER BY documentary_awards DESC;

-- Headline report: the qualifying universities and their award totals.
SELECT university_name,
       country,
       documentary_awards
FROM selections
ORDER BY documentary_awards DESC,
         university_name;

-- Award totals per country, restricted to the qualifying universities.
SELECT country,
       COUNT(*) AS qualifying_universities,
       SUM(documentary_awards) AS country_awards
FROM selections
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY country_awards DESC;

-- Senior documentary films that earned awards at the qualifying universities.
SELECT selections.university_name,
       student_directors.director_name,
       festival_submissions.film_title,
       festival_submissions.festival_name,
       festival_submissions.awards_won
FROM selections
JOIN universities
    ON universities.university_name = selections.university_name
   AND universities.country = selections.country
JOIN student_directors
    ON student_directors.university_id = universities.university_id
JOIN festival_submissions
    ON festival_submissions.director_id = student_directors.director_id
WHERE festival_submissions.genre = 'Documentary'
  AND student_directors.study_year = 'Senior'
  AND festival_submissions.awards_won > 0
ORDER BY selections.documentary_awards DESC,
         festival_submissions.awards_won DESC;

text_es: Create a procedure `qualifiers()` that finds the school districts with the strongest spelling bee contestants. The database has tables for districts, schools, and contestant scores. Join the tables to calculate the average vocabulary score for each district. Filter the dataset to include only middle school contestants and scores from the regional finals. Group the records by the district name and the state. Show only the districts where the average score is above ninety five. Sort the output from highest to lowest average score.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE districts (
    district_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    district_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    state CHAR(2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE schools (
    school_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    district_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES districts (district_id),
    school_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    school_level VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE contestants (
    contestant_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    school_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES schools (school_id),
    full_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    grade TINYINT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE contestant_scores (
    score_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    contestant_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES contestants (contestant_id),
    round_name VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    vocabulary_score DECIMAL(5, 2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW district_finals_averages AS
SELECT d.district_name,
       d.state,
       AVG(sc.vocabulary_score) AS avg_vocabulary_score,
       COUNT(*) AS scores_counted
FROM contestant_scores sc
JOIN contestants c
    ON c.contestant_id = sc.contestant_id
JOIN schools s
    ON s.school_id = c.school_id
JOIN districts d
    ON d.district_id = s.district_id
WHERE s.school_level = 'Middle School'
  AND sc.round_name = 'Regional Finals'
GROUP BY d.district_name, d.state
HAVING AVG(sc.vocabulary_score) > 95;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE qualifiers()
BEGIN
    SELECT district_name, state,
           avg_vocabulary_score, scores_counted
    FROM district_finals_averages
    ORDER BY avg_vocabulary_score DESC;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE qualifying_contestants(IN in_state CHAR(2))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.full_name, s.school_name,
           d.district_name, q.avg_vocabulary_score,
           sc.vocabulary_score
    FROM contestants c
    JOIN schools s
        ON s.school_id = c.school_id
    JOIN districts d
        ON d.district_id = s.district_id
    JOIN contestant_scores sc
        ON sc.contestant_id = c.contestant_id
    JOIN district_finals_averages q
        ON q.district_name = d.district_name
        AND q.state = d.state
    WHERE d.state = in_state
      AND s.school_level = 'Middle School'
      AND sc.round_name = 'Regional Finals'
    ORDER BY sc.vocabulary_score DESC, c.full_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL qualifiers();
CALL qualifying_contestants('OH');

text_es: Write a query `endurance` that identifies the most active marathon training clubs. You have tables for city zones, training clubs, and runner mileage logs. Connect these tables to sum the total miles run by each club. Limit the data to weekend long runs and runners preparing for a full marathon. Group the results by the club name and their home zone. Keep only the clubs that have logged a combined total of over ten thousand miles. Order the final list by the total miles in descending order.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE city_zones (
    zone_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    zone_name   VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE training_clubs (
    club_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    club_name   VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    zone_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES city_zones (zone_id)
);

CREATE TABLE mileage_logs (
    log_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    club_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES training_clubs (club_id),
    runner_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    run_date    DATE NOT NULL,
    day_type    VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    race_goal   VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    miles       NUMERIC(6, 2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW endurance AS
SELECT
    tc.club_name AS club,
    cz.zone_name AS home_zone,
    SUM(ml.miles) AS total_miles
FROM mileage_logs ml
JOIN training_clubs tc
    ON tc.club_id = ml.club_id
JOIN city_zones cz
    ON cz.zone_id = tc.zone_id
WHERE ml.day_type = 'weekend long run'
    AND ml.race_goal = 'full marathon'
GROUP BY
    tc.club_name,
    cz.zone_name
HAVING SUM(ml.miles) > 10000
ORDER BY total_miles DESC;

CREATE VIEW zone_endurance AS
SELECT
    home_zone,
    COUNT(*) AS qualifying_clubs,
    SUM(total_miles) AS zone_miles
FROM endurance
GROUP BY home_zone;

CREATE VIEW club_weekend_rosters AS
SELECT
    tc.club_name AS club,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ml.runner_name) AS marathoners
FROM mileage_logs ml
JOIN training_clubs tc
    ON tc.club_id = ml.club_id
WHERE ml.day_type = 'weekend long run'
    AND ml.race_goal = 'full marathon'
GROUP BY tc.club_name;

SELECT
    e.club,
    e.home_zone,
    e.total_miles,
    r.marathoners,
    ROUND(e.total_miles / r.marathoners, 1) AS miles_per_runner
FROM endurance e
JOIN club_weekend_rosters r
    ON r.club = e.club
ORDER BY e.total_miles DESC;

SELECT
    z.home_zone,
    z.qualifying_clubs,
    z.zone_miles
FROM zone_endurance z
WHERE z.qualifying_clubs > 1
ORDER BY z.zone_miles DESC;

text_es: Create a view `attendance` that lists historic houses with the highest visitor turnout. The system contains tables for counties, historic houses, and daily visitor logs. Join the tables to calculate the total number of visitors for each house. Filter the entries to only include guided tours and houses built before the nineteenth century. Group the data by the house name and the county it resides in. Retain only houses that received over five thousand visitors this year. Sort the output by the visitor count descending.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE counties (
    county_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    county_name    VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    region         VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE historic_houses (
    house_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    house_name     VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    county_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES counties (county_id),
    year_built     INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE visitor_logs (
    log_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    house_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES historic_houses (house_id),
    visit_date     DATE NOT NULL,
    tour_type      VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    visitor_count  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW attendance AS
SELECT
    h.house_name,
    c.county_name,
    SUM(v.visitor_count) AS total_visitors
FROM historic_houses h
JOIN counties c
    ON h.county_id = c.county_id
JOIN visitor_logs v
    ON v.house_id = h.house_id
WHERE v.tour_type = 'guided'
    AND h.year_built < 1800
    AND v.visit_date >= DATE_TRUNC('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY h.house_name, c.county_name
HAVING SUM(v.visitor_count) > 5000
ORDER BY total_visitors DESC;

SELECT
    a.county_name,
    COUNT(*) AS popular_houses,
    SUM(a.total_visitors) AS county_visitors
FROM attendance a
GROUP BY a.county_name
ORDER BY county_visitors DESC;

SELECT
    a.house_name,
    a.county_name,
    c.region,
    h.year_built,
    a.total_visitors
FROM attendance a
JOIN historic_houses h
    ON h.house_name = a.house_name
JOIN counties c
    ON c.county_id = h.county_id
    AND c.county_name = a.county_name
WHERE c.region = 'North West'
ORDER BY a.total_visitors DESC;

SELECT
    a.house_name,
    a.total_visitors,
    ROUND(a.total_visitors * 100.0 / t.grand_total, 2) AS share_percent
FROM attendance a
CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT
        SUM(total_visitors) AS grand_total
    FROM attendance
) t
WHERE a.total_visitors > 10000
ORDER BY share_percent DESC;

SELECT
    a.house_name,
    v.tour_type,
    SUM(v.visitor_count) AS logged_visitors
FROM attendance a
JOIN historic_houses h
    ON h.house_name = a.house_name
JOIN visitor_logs v
    ON v.house_id = h.house_id
WHERE v.visit_date >= DATE_TRUNC('year', CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY a.house_name, v.tour_type
ORDER BY a.house_name, logged_visitors DESC;

text_es: Write a procedure `excellence()` that highlights the most consistent amateur bakers. Use tables for competition categories, registered bakers, and judge evaluations. Link the tables to find the average presentation score for each baker. Filter the data to include only pastry categories and bakers who have entered at least three competitions. Group the findings by the baker name and their home town. Show only the bakers who maintain an average presentation score above eight out of ten. Order the list by the average score from highest to lowest.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE competition_categories (
    category_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    category_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    category_type VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE registered_bakers (
    baker_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    baker_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    home_town  VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE judge_evaluations (
    evaluation_id      INT PRIMARY KEY,
    baker_id           INT NOT NULL,
    category_id        INT NOT NULL,
    competition_id     INT NOT NULL,
    presentation_score DECIMAL(3,1),
    FOREIGN KEY (baker_id) REFERENCES registered_bakers (baker_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES competition_categories (category_id)
);

CREATE VIEW pastry_entries AS
SELECT
    e.baker_id,
    e.competition_id,
    e.presentation_score
FROM
    judge_evaluations AS e
JOIN
    competition_categories AS c
ON
    e.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE
    c.category_type = 'Pastry'
AND
    e.presentation_score IS NOT NULL;

CREATE VIEW pastry_entry_counts AS
SELECT
    baker_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT competition_id) AS competitions_entered
FROM
    pastry_entries
GROUP BY
    baker_id;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE excellence()
BEGIN
    SELECT
        b.baker_name AS baker,
        b.home_town AS town,
        ROUND(AVG(p.presentation_score), 2) AS avg_presentation
    FROM
        registered_bakers AS b
    JOIN
        pastry_entries AS p
    ON
        p.baker_id = b.baker_id
    JOIN
        pastry_entry_counts AS k
    ON
        k.baker_id = b.baker_id
    WHERE
        k.competitions_entered >= 3
    GROUP BY
        b.baker_name,
        b.home_town
    HAVING
        AVG(p.presentation_score) > 8
    ORDER BY
        avg_presentation DESC;
END //

DELIMITER ;

text_es: Implement `analyze(logs)` to calculate timber processing volumes at a lumber mill. The database features a tree species table and a processed logs table. Join them by matching the tree identifier to the origin tree. Filter to keep only morning shift logs where the length is greater than ten feet. Group by species name, select it, and sum the volumes as total volume, ordering by total volume in descending order. For example, oak logs of twenty and thirty cubic feet yield oak with total volume fifty.
text_nat:
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS "analyze";
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS eligible_logs;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS processed_logs;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tree_species;

CREATE TABLE tree_species (
    tree_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    species_name TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE processed_logs (
    log_id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    origin_tree       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tree_species (tree_id),
    shift             TEXT NOT NULL,
    length_feet       NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    volume_cubic_feet NUMERIC NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW eligible_logs AS
SELECT
    L.log_id,
    S.species_name,
    L.length_feet,
    L.volume_cubic_feet
FROM
    processed_logs AS L
JOIN
    tree_species AS S
    ON L.origin_tree = S.tree_id
WHERE LOWER(TRIM(L.shift)) = 'morning'
    AND L.length_feet > 10;

CREATE VIEW "analyze" AS
SELECT
    species_name,
    SUM(volume_cubic_feet) AS total_volume
FROM eligible_logs
GROUP BY species_name
ORDER BY total_volume DESC;

text_es: Implement `report(bouts)` to review sumo wrestling tournament bouts. The database stores a wrestlers table and a match results table. Join them by matching the athlete number to the fighter identifier. Filter to include only top division bouts where the match duration exceeded two minutes. Group by winning technique, select it, and count the victories as total wins, ordering by total wins descending. For example, two lengthy top division bouts won by a push out result in push out with total wins two.
text_nat:
-- Schema: wrestlers roster and the recorded bout outcomes of a tournament.
CREATE TABLE wrestlers (
    athlete_no INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    ring_name  TEXT NOT NULL,
    division   TEXT NOT NULL,
    heya       TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE match_results (
    bout_id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    fighter_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wrestlers (athlete_no),
    opponent_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wrestlers (athlete_no),
    winning_technique TEXT NOT NULL,
    duration_seconds  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    tournament_day    INTEGER NOT NULL
);

    (2, 'Kotoseiryu', 'Makuuchi', 'Sadogatake'),
    (3, 'Hoshoryu',   'Makuuchi', 'Tatsunami'),
    (4, 'Chiyomaru',  'Juryo',    'Kokonoe');
INSERT INTO match_results VALUES
    (101, 1, 2, 'push out',  185, 1),
    (102, 3, 2, 'push out',  212, 2),
    (103, 2, 1, 'throw',     240, 3),
    (104, 1, 3, 'slap down',  45, 4),
    (105, 4, 1, 'push out',  300, 5),
    (106, 3, 1, 'throw',     150, 6);

-- Qualifying bouts: top division winners whose match lasted over two minutes.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION lengthy_top_bouts(bouts match_results[])
RETURNS TABLE (bout_id INTEGER, ring_name TEXT, winning_technique TEXT, duration_seconds INTEGER)
language sql
AS $$
    SELECT b.bout_id,
           w.ring_name,
           b.winning_technique,
           b.duration_seconds
    FROM unnest(bouts) b
    JOIN wrestlers w
      ON w.athlete_no = b.fighter_id
    WHERE w.division = 'Makuuchi'
      AND b.duration_seconds > 120
$$;
-- Bouts that cannot be reported on: unregistered fighter or impossible duration.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION invalid_bouts(bouts match_results[])
RETURNS TABLE (bout_id INTEGER, problem TEXT)
language sql
AS $$
    SELECT b.bout_id,
           CASE WHEN w.athlete_no IS NULL THEN 'unknown fighter' ELSE 'bad duration' END AS problem
    FROM unnest(bouts) b
    LEFT JOIN wrestlers w
           ON w.athlete_no = b.fighter_id
    WHERE w.athlete_no IS NULL
       OR b.duration_seconds < 0
$$;
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION report(bouts match_results[])
RETURNS TABLE (winning_technique TEXT, total_wins BIGINT)
language sql
AS $$
    SELECT t.winning_technique,
           COUNT(*) AS total_wins
    FROM lengthy_top_bouts(bouts) t
    GROUP BY t.winning_technique
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
$$;

-- Driver: review the stored tournament.
CREATE VIEW tournament AS
SELECT array_agg(m) bouts
FROM match_results m;
SELECT v.bout_id,
       v.problem
FROM tournament t
CROSS JOIN LATERAL invalid_bouts(t.bouts) v
ORDER BY v.bout_id;
SELECT r.winning_technique,
       r.total_wins
FROM tournament t
CROSS JOIN LATERAL report(t.bouts) r
ORDER BY r.total_wins DESC;

text_es: Implement `summarize(sessions)` to review ice skating rink zamboni operations. The database contains rink schedules and resurfacing logs tables. Join them by matching the block code to the time block. Filter for public skating sessions where the water volume used was over one hundred gallons. Group by zamboni driver name, select it, and count the resurfacing runs as total runs, ordering descending by total runs. For example, driver john completing two heavy water runs yields john with total runs two.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE rink_schedules (
    schedule_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    block_code   TEXT NOT NULL,
    session_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    rink_name    TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE resurfacing_logs (
    log_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    time_block    TEXT NOT NULL,
    driver_name   TEXT NOT NULL,
    water_gallons NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    run_date      DATE NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW heavy_public_runs AS
SELECT
    l.log_id,
    l.driver_name,
    l.water_gallons,
    l.run_date,
    s.rink_name
FROM
    resurfacing_logs AS l
JOIN
    rink_schedules AS s
    ON l.time_block = s.block_code
WHERE
    s.session_type = 'public skating'
AND
    l.water_gallons > 100;

CREATE VIEW summarize AS
SELECT
    driver_name,
    COUNT(*) AS total_runs
FROM
    heavy_public_runs
GROUP BY
    driver_name
ORDER BY
    total_runs DESC;

CREATE VIEW driver_workload_report AS
SELECT
    r.driver_name,
    r.total_runs,
    h.rink_name,
    SUM(h.water_gallons) AS gallons_used
FROM
    summarize AS r
JOIN
    heavy_public_runs AS h
    ON r.driver_name = h.driver_name
GROUP BY
    r.driver_name,
    r.total_runs,
    h.rink_name
ORDER BY
    r.total_runs DESC;

text_es: Write a script `utilization(database)` that analyzes rental patterns across three tables: vehicles with identifier, make, model, and purchase year; branches with branch identifier, city, and capacity; and rentals linking vehicle and branch identifiers with start date, end date, and total revenue. First, create a view that calculates the total revenue and total days rented for each vehicle. Then, write a query that retrieves the branch city, vehicle make, and total revenue for vehicles purchased after two thousand eighteen that generated more than five thousand in revenue and were rented for over thirty days. Sort the final output alphabetically by branch city, then by total revenue from highest to lowest. Example input: a branch in Chicago, a Ford vehicle purchased in two thousand nineteen, rented for forty days generating six thousand. Example output: Chicago, Ford, six thousand.
text_nat:
-- utilization(database): rental utilization analysis over vehicles, branches and rentals.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vehicle_utilization;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS rentals;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS branches;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS vehicles;

CREATE TABLE vehicles (
    vehicle_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    make           TEXT NOT NULL,
    model          TEXT NOT NULL,
    purchase_year  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE branches (
    branch_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    city       TEXT NOT NULL,
    capacity   INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE rentals (
    rental_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicles (vehicle_id),
    branch_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES branches (branch_id),
    start_date     TEXT NOT NULL,
    end_date       TEXT NOT NULL,
    total_revenue  NUMERIC NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW vehicle_utilization
AS
SELECT
    v.vehicle_id,
    v.make,
    v.model,
    v.purchase_year,
    sum(r.total_revenue) AS lifetime_revenue,
    sum(julianday(r.end_date) - julianday(r.start_date)) AS days_rented
FROM vehicles v
JOIN rentals r
ON r.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
GROUP BY
    v.vehicle_id,
    v.make,
    v.model,
    v.purchase_year;

SELECT

    u.make AS vehicle_make,

FROM rentals r
JOIN vehicle_utilization u
ON u.vehicle_id = r.vehicle_id
JOIN branches b
ON b.branch_id = r.branch_id
WHERE u.purchase_year > 2018

text_es: Create a reporting script `efficiency(database)` for surgical outcomes. The medical database has surgeons with identifier, full name, and specialty, surgeries with identifier, surgeon identifier, procedure name, and duration in minutes, and outcomes linking surgery identifier to patient recovery days and complication flag. Build a view that averages the duration and recovery days for each surgeon. Write a subsequent query that joins surgeons, their average metrics, and counts of surgeries with complications. Select the surgeon full name, specialty, average duration, and total complications for those specializing in cardiology who have an average duration under one hundred twenty minutes and fewer than three total complications. Sort by total complications ascending, then average duration ascending. Example input: surgeon Bob in cardiology, average duration ninety minutes, one complication. Example output: Bob, cardiology, ninety, one.
text_nat:
-- efficiency(database): surgical outcome efficiency report

CREATE TABLE Surgeons (
    surgeon_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    full_name  TEXT NOT NULL,
    specialty  TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Surgeries (
    surgery_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    surgeon_id       INTEGER REFERENCES Surgeons (surgeon_id),
    procedure_name   TEXT NOT NULL,
    duration_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Outcomes (
    surgery_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES Surgeries (surgery_id),
    recovery_days INTEGER NOT NULL,
    complication  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

    (10, 1, 'bypass', 80), (11, 1, 'valve repair', 100),
    (12, 2, 'transplant', 150), (13, 3, 'bypass', 95),
    (14, 3, 'bypass', 105), (15, 3, 'valve repair', 90),
    (16, 4, 'craniotomy', 200);

    (10, 6, 0), (11, 12, 1), (12, 20, 1), (13, 14, 1),
    (14, 15, 1), (15, 11, 1), (16, 30, 0);

-- Average duration and recovery time per surgeon
CREATE VIEW SurgeonAverages AS
SELECT
    Surgeries.surgeon_id,
    AVG(Surgeries.duration_minutes) AS avg_duration,
    AVG(Outcomes.recovery_days) AS avg_recovery_days
FROM Surgeries
LEFT JOIN Outcomes
    ON Outcomes.surgery_id = Surgeries.surgery_id
GROUP BY Surgeries.surgeon_id;

-- Complication totals per surgeon
CREATE VIEW SurgeonComplications AS
SELECT
    Surgeries.surgeon_id,
    SUM(Outcomes.complication) AS total_complications
FROM Surgeries
LEFT JOIN Outcomes
    ON Outcomes.surgery_id = Surgeries.surgery_id
GROUP BY Surgeries.surgeon_id;

-- Efficient cardiology surgeons
SELECT
    Surgeons.full_name,
    Surgeons.specialty,
    SurgeonAverages.avg_duration,
    SurgeonComplications.total_complications
FROM Surgeons
JOIN SurgeonAverages
    ON SurgeonAverages.surgeon_id = Surgeons.surgeon_id
JOIN SurgeonComplications
    ON SurgeonComplications.surgeon_id = Surgeons.surgeon_id
WHERE Surgeons.specialty = 'cardiology'
  AND SurgeonAverages.avg_duration < 120
  AND SurgeonComplications.total_complications < 3
ORDER BY SurgeonComplications.total_complications ASC,

text_es: Develop `ranking(database)` to evaluate top real estate agents. The property database contains agents with identifier, full name, and office location, properties with identifier, agent identifier, listing price, and sale price, and transactions recording property identifier, closing date, and buyer name. Form a view that aggregates total sales volume and count of properties sold for each agent. Write a query that retrieves the agent full name, office location, total sales volume, and average sale to list price ratio for agents in the downtown office who have sold more than five properties and achieved a total volume over two million. Order the final report by total sales volume descending. Example input: downtown agent Clara, six properties sold, three million volume, ninety eight percent ratio. Example output: Clara, downtown, three million, ninety eight percent.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE agents (
    agent_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    full_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    office_location TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE properties (
    property_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    agent_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES agents (agent_id),
    listing_price NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    sale_price NUMERIC

Write a query to find suppliers in the northwest region providing dairy ingredients who delivered over one thousand units but have more than five rejected deliveries. text_es: Write `graduations(database)` to track student progress. The learning system features students with identifier, full name, and enrollment date, modules with identifier, course name, and required passing score, and assessments recording student identifier, module identifier, attempt date, and achieved score. Build a view that finds the highest score each student achieved for each module. Write a query that selects the student full name, course name, and highest score for students who enrolled in the current year and achieved a score greater than or equal to the required passing score on their first or second attempt. Order the output by course name ascending, then highest score descending. Example input: student Emma enrolled this year, course Python, required eighty, achieved ninety. Example output: Emma, Python, ninety.
text_nat:
-- Learning management schema: students, modules, and assessment attempts.
CREATE TABLE students (
    student_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    full_name       TEXT NOT NULL,
    enrollment_date DATE NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE modules (
    module_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    course_name    TEXT NOT NULL,
    passing_score  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE assessments (
    student_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES students (student_id),
    module_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES modules (module_id),
    attempt_date DATE NOT NULL,
    score        INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (student_id, module_id, attempt_date)
);

-- Numbers every attempt chronologically within a student/module pair.
CREATE VIEW ranked_attempts AS
SELECT
    a.student_id,
    a.module_id,
    a.attempt_date,
    a.score,
    COUNT(p.attempt_date) + 1 AS attempt_number
FROM assessments a
LEFT JOIN assessments p
       ON p.student_id = a.student_id
      AND p.module_id = a.module_id
      AND p.attempt_date < a.attempt_date
GROUP BY a.student_id,
         a.module_id,
         a.attempt_date,
         a.score;

-- Required view: the highest score each student achieved for each module.
CREATE VIEW best_module_scores AS
SELECT
    a.student_id,
    a.module_id,
    MAX(a.score) AS highest_score
FROM assessments a
GROUP BY a.student_id,
         a.module_id;

-- Early passes: a module cleared on the first or second attempt.
CREATE VIEW early_passes AS
SELECT DISTINCT
    r.student_id,
    r.module_id
FROM ranked_attempts r
JOIN modules m
     ON m.module_id = r.module_id
WHERE r.attempt_number <= 2
  AND r.score >= m.passing_score;

SELECT

FROM best_module_scores b
JOIN students s

JOIN modules m

JOIN early_passes e

WHERE strftime('%Y', s.enrollment_date) = strftime('%Y', 'now')

text_es: Develop `congestion(database)` to monitor shipping delays. The maritime database has ships with identifier, vessel name, and home port, containers with identifier, ship identifier, destination port, and weight, and voyages recording ship identifier, departure date, expected arrival date, and actual arrival date. Set up a view that calculates the total container weight and average delay in days for each ship. Write a final query retrieving the vessel name, home port, total weight, and average delay for ships bound for international ports that have an average delay greater than two days and carry more than ten thousand tons. Sort by average delay descending, then vessel name. Example input: ship Oceanic from Seattle, twenty thousand tons, three days delay. Example output: Oceanic, Seattle, twenty thousand, three.
text_nat:
-- congestion(database): maritime shipping delay monitor

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS voyage_delays;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS voyages;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS containers;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ships;

CREATE TABLE ships (ship_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, vessel_name TEXT NOT NULL, home_port TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE ports (port_name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, country TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE containers (container_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ship_id INTEGER REFERENCES ships (ship_id),
    destination_port TEXT REFERENCES ports (port_name), weight_tons REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE voyages (voyage_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ship_id INTEGER REFERENCES ships (ship_id),
    departure_date TEXT NOT NULL, expected_arrival TEXT NOT NULL, actual_arrival TEXT);

CREATE VIEW voyage_delays AS
SELECT
    ship_id,
    AVG(JULIANDAY(actual_arrival) - JULIANDAY(expected_arrival)) AS avg_delay
FROM
    voyages
WHERE
    actual_arrival IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
    ship_id;

CREATE VIEW ship_congestion AS
SELECT
    s.ship_id,
    s.vessel_name,
    s.home_port,
    SUM(c.weight_tons) AS total_weight,
    d.avg_delay,
    MAX(p.country <> 'United States') AS international_bound
FROM
    ships AS s
JOIN
    containers AS c
    ON c.ship_id = s.ship_id
JOIN
    ports AS p
    ON p.port_name = c.destination_port
JOIN
    voyage_delays AS d
    ON d.ship_id = s.ship_id
GROUP BY

    d.avg_delay;

WHERE
    sc.avg_delay > 2
    AND sc.total_weight > 10000
    AND sc.international_bound = 1
ORDER BY
    sc.avg_delay DESC,
    sc.vessel_name;

text_es: Implement `reviews(database)` to evaluate hotel performance. The hospitality database features hotels with identifier, property name, and star rating, stays with identifier, hotel identifier, guest name, and checkout date, and ratings linking stay identifier to numeric score and text comment. Construct a view that calculates the average numeric score and total number of ratings for each hotel. Create a query that retrieves the property name, star rating, average score, and total ratings for five star hotels that have an average score below four and more than fifty total ratings. Order the output by average score ascending, then total ratings descending. Example input: hotel Grand Plaza, five stars, average score three point eight, sixty ratings. Example output: Grand Plaza, five stars, three point eight, sixty.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE hotels (
    hotel_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    property_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    star_rating INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE stays (
    stay_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    hotel_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES hotels (hotel_id),
    guest_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    checkout_date DATE NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE ratings (
    stay_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES stays (stay_id),
    score NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    comment TEXT
);

CREATE VIEW hotel_rating_summary
AS
SELECT
    h.hotel_id, h.property_name, h.star_rating,
    AVG(r.score) AS average_score,
    COUNT(r.stay_id) AS total_ratings
FROM
    hotels AS h
    JOIN
    stays AS s
        ON s.hotel_id = h.hotel_id
    JOIN
    ratings AS r
        ON r.stay_id = s.stay_id
GROUP BY
    h.hotel_id, h.property_name, h.star_rating;

INSERT INTO hotels (hotel_id, property_name, star_rating)
VALUES (1, 'Grand Plaza', 5);

INSERT INTO stays (stay_id, hotel_id, guest_name, checkout_date)
WITH RECURSIVE seq (n)
AS (
    SELECT 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT n + 1
    FROM seq
    WHERE n < 60
)
SELECT
    n, 1, 'Guest ' || n, DATE('2024-01-01', '+' || n || ' days')
FROM
    seq;

INSERT INTO ratings (stay_id, score, comment)
SELECT
    s.stay_id,
    CASE
        WHEN s.stay_id <= 12 THEN 3
        ELSE 4
    END,
    'Comfortable room, slow check-in'
FROM
    stays AS s
WHERE
    s.hotel_id = 1;

SELECT
    property_name, star_rating, average_score, total_ratings
FROM
    hotel_rating_summary
WHERE
    star_rating = 5
    AND average_score < 4
    AND total_ratings > 50
ORDER BY
    average_score ASC,
    total_ratings DESC;

text_es: Implement `rewards(database)` to calculate driver bonuses. The delivery database includes drivers with identifier, full name, and vehicle type, routes with identifier, zone, and base pay, and deliveries recording driver identifier, route identifier, delivery date, and on time status. Build a view that counts the total deliveries and the number of on time deliveries for each driver. Write a query returning the full name, vehicle type, total deliveries, and on time percentage for drivers using electric vans who completed at least one hundred deliveries with an on time percentage above ninety five. Order the results by on time percentage descending, then full name. Example input: driver Helen, electric van, one hundred twenty deliveries, ninety eight percent on time. Example output: Helen, electric van, one hundred twenty, ninety eight percent.
text_nat:
-- rewards(database): driver bonus module for the delivery database.

CREATE TABLE drivers (
    driver_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    full_name     TEXT    NOT NULL,
    vehicle_type  TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE routes (
    route_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    zone      TEXT    NOT NULL,
    base_pay  NUMERIC NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE deliveries (
    delivery_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    driver_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES drivers(driver_id),
    route_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES routes(route_id),
    delivery_date TEXT    NOT NULL,
    on_time       INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW driver_delivery_counts AS
SELECT driver_id,
       COUNT(*) total_deliveries,
       SUM(CASE WHEN on_time = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) on_time_deliveries
FROM deliveries
GROUP BY driver_id;

INSERT INTO drivers (driver_id, full_name, vehicle_type) VALUES
    (1, 'Helen', 'electric van'),
    (2, 'Ravi',  'electric van'),
    (3, 'Mia',   'diesel van');

INSERT INTO routes (route_id, zone, base_pay) VALUES
    (1, 'north', 42.00),
    (2, 'south', 38.50),
    (3, 'central', 45.25);

INSERT INTO deliveries (driver_id, route_id, delivery_date, on_time)
WITH RECURSIVE seq(i) AS (
    SELECT 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT i + 1
    FROM seq
    WHERE i < 120
)
SELECT 1,
       1 + (i % 3),
       DATE('2024-01-01', '+' || i || ' day'),
       CASE WHEN i % 60 = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
FROM seq;

INSERT INTO deliveries (driver_id, route_id, delivery_date, on_time)
WITH RECURSIVE seq(i) AS (
    SELECT 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT i + 1
    FROM seq
    WHERE i < 110
)
SELECT 2,
       1 + (i % 2),
       DATE('2024-02-01', '+' || i || ' day'),
       CASE WHEN i % 8 = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
FROM seq;

SELECT d.full_name,
       d.vehicle_type,
       c.total_deliveries,
       ROUND(100.0 * c.on_time_deliveries / c.total_deliveries, 1) AS on_time_pct
FROM drivers d
JOIN driver_delivery_counts c
    ON c.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE d.vehicle_type = 'electric van'
  AND c.total_deliveries >= 100
  AND 100.0 * c.on_time_deliveries / c.total_deliveries > 95
ORDER BY on_time_pct DESC,
         d.full_name;

SELECT d.full_name,
       r.zone,
       ROUND(0.05 * SUM(r.base_pay), 2) AS bonus_amount
FROM drivers d
JOIN deliveries dl
    ON dl.driver_id = d.driver_id
JOIN routes r
    ON r.route_id = dl.route_id
JOIN driver_delivery_counts c
    ON c.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE d.vehicle_type = 'electric van'
  AND dl.on_time = 1
  AND c.total_deliveries >= 100
  AND 100.0 * c.on_time_deliveries / c.total_deliveries > 95
GROUP BY d.full_name,
         r.zone
ORDER BY bonus_amount DESC,
         d.full_name;

text_es: Implement a SQL procedure `restock(minimum)` that identifies rare potion ingredients running low across alchemist shops. A table of ingredients stores the identifier, ingredient name, and magical property, while a table of inventories holds the shop identifier, ingredient identifier, and quantity in stock. Combine the ingredients and inventories tables to sum the total quantity of each ingredient across all shops. Filter out any ingredients whose magical property is healing or protection. Group by the ingredient name and select only those where the total quantity is below the provided minimum. Return the ingredient name and total quantity, ordering by quantity ascending. Example input: minimum 50. Example output: (dragon scales, 12), (mandrake root, 34).
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE ingredients (
    ingredient_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ingredient_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    magical_property VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE inventories (
    shop_id INT NOT NULL,
    ingredient_id INT NOT NULL,
    quantity INT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (shop_id, ingredient_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (ingredient_id) REFERENCES ingredients (ingredient_id)
);

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE restock(IN minimum INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT
        i.ingredient_name
        AS ingredient,
        SUM(v.quantity)
        AS total_quantity
    FROM ingredients
        AS i
    JOIN inventories
        AS v
        ON v.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id
    WHERE i.magical_property <> 'healing'
        AND i.magical_property <> 'protection'
    GROUP BY
        i.ingredient_name
    HAVING SUM(v.quantity) < minimum
    ORDER BY
        total_quantity ASC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE restock_orders(IN minimum INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT
        v.shop_id,
        i.ingredient_name
        AS ingredient,
        v.quantity
        AS shop_quantity,
        low.total_quantity
    FROM (
        SELECT
            i2.ingredient_id,
            SUM(v2.quantity)
            AS total_quantity
        FROM ingredients
            AS i2
        JOIN inventories
            AS v2
            ON v2.ingredient_id = i2.ingredient_id
        WHERE i2.magical_property <> 'healing'
            AND i2.magical_property <> 'protection'
        GROUP BY
            i2.ingredient_id
        HAVING SUM(v2.quantity) < minimum
    ) AS low
    JOIN ingredients
        AS i
        ON i.ingredient_id = low.ingredient_id
    JOIN inventories
        AS v
        ON v.ingredient_id = low.ingredient_id
        AND v.quantity > 0
    ORDER BY
        low.total_quantity ASC,
        v.quantity ASC;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL restock(50);
CALL restock_orders(50);

text_es: Write a SQL procedure `secure(breaches)` that flags wildlife preserves failing to contain dangerous creatures. A preserves table contains the identifier, region, and warden name, and a breach log table records the preserve identifier, creature type, and severity level. Join the tables to count the total number of breaches per warden. Ignore breaches involving harmless creatures like pixies or fairies. Group by the region and warden name, and return the region, warden name, and total breaches for wardens who have a total breach count higher than the breaches parameter. Order the results by total breaches descending. Example input: breaches 3. Example output: (black forest, hagrid, 7).
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE preserves (
    preserve_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    region VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    warden VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE breach_log (
    breach_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    preserve_id INT NOT NULL,
    creature_type VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    severity INT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE harmless_creatures (
    creature_type VARCHAR(60) PRIMARY KEY
);

INSERT INTO harmless_creatures (creature_type) VALUES ('pixie'), ('fairy');

INSERT INTO preserves (preserve_id, region, warden) VALUES
    (1, 'black forest', 'hagrid'),
    (2, 'black forest', 'hagrid'),
    (3, 'highland fen', 'mcgonagall'),
    (4, 'dragon coast', 'charlie');

INSERT INTO breach_log (breach_id, preserve_id, creature_type, severity) VALUES
    (1, 1, 'acromantula', 4),
    (2, 1, 'dragon', 5),
    (3, 1, 'hippogriff', 3),
    (4, 1, 'pixie', 1),
    (5, 2, 'dragon', 5),
    (6, 2, 'manticore', 5),
    (7, 2, 'werewolf', 4),
    (8, 2, 'chimaera', 5),
    (9, 2, 'fairy', 1),
    (10, 3, 'grindylow', 2),
    (11, 3, 'kelpie', 3),
    (12, 4, 'dragon', 5);

CREATE VIEW dangerous_breaches AS
SELECT
    p.region AS region,
    p.warden AS warden,
    b.creature_type AS creature_type
FROM preserves
    AS p
JOIN breach_log
    AS b
    ON b.preserve_id = p.preserve_id
WHERE b.creature_type NOT IN (
    SELECT creature_type
    FROM harmless_creatures
);

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE secure(IN breaches INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT
        d.region AS region,
        d.warden AS warden,
        COUNT(*) AS total_breaches
    FROM dangerous_breaches
        AS d
    GROUP BY
        d.region,
        d.warden
    HAVING COUNT(*) > breaches
    ORDER BY total_breaches DESC;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL secure(3);

text_es: Create a reporting function `audit(springs, incidents)` to review recreational safety metrics. The inputs represent trampoline equipment logs and customer injury reports. Connect the equipment logs to the injury reports using the zone identifier. Retain only the records where springs were not replaced within two years and the incident involved an adult jumper. Group the data by the park zone name to count the total number of safety incidents. Arrange the output list by the incident count in descending order. Example input: the dodgeball zone with old springs and one adult incident. Example output: the text dodgeball zone and a count of one.
text_nat:
-- Recreational safety audit module: trampoline spring logs vs. customer injury reports.

CREATE TABLE springs (
    zone_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    zone_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_spring_replacement TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE incidents (
    incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    zone_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    jumper_age INTEGER NOT NULL,
    injury_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    incident_date TEXT NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO springs (zone_id, zone_name, last_spring_replacement) VALUES
    (1, 'dodgeball zone', '2019-04-11'),
    (2, 'foam pit zone', '2024-08-02'),
    (3, 'main court zone', NULL);

INSERT INTO incidents (incident_id, zone_id, jumper_age, injury_type, incident_date) VALUES
    (1, 1, 34, 'sprained ankle', '2025-05-02'),
    (2, 1, 9, 'bruised elbow', '2025-05-07'),
    (3, 2, 41, 'wrist strain', '2025-06-15'),
    (4, 3, 27, 'knee injury', '2025-07-01'),
    (5, 3, 52, 'shoulder injury', '2025-07-19'),
    (6, 9, 30, 'back strain', '2025-07-20');

-- audit(springs, incidents): adult incidents in zones whose springs are older than two years.
CREATE VIEW audit AS
SELECT
    s.zone_name AS park_zone,
    COUNT(i.incident_id) AS incident_count
FROM
    springs AS s
JOIN
    incidents AS i
    ON i.zone_id = s.zone_id
WHERE
    i.jumper_age >= 18
    AND (
        s.last_spring_replacement IS NULL
        OR s.last_spring_replacement < DATE('now', '-2 years')
    )
GROUP BY
    s.zone_name
ORDER BY
    incident_count DESC;

-- Injury reports whose zone identifier does not exist in the equipment logs cannot be audited.
CREATE VIEW orphan_incidents AS
SELECT
    i.incident_id,
    i.zone_id AS unknown_zone_id,
    i.incident_date
FROM
    incidents AS i
LEFT JOIN
    springs AS s
    ON s.zone_id = i.zone_id
WHERE
    s.zone_id IS NULL;

-- Driver: print the audit report, then the unmatched injury reports.
SELECT
    park_zone,
    incident_count
FROM
    audit;

SELECT
    o.incident_id,
    o.unknown_zone_id,
    o.incident_date
FROM
    orphan_incidents AS o
ORDER BY
    o.incident_date,
    o.incident_id;

text_es: Formulate a query using `tally(models, logs)` to track artisan craftsmanship hours. The inputs are clock design specifications and artisan time logs. Link the designs to the time logs using the model identifier. Restrict the data to black forest traditional models and carving sessions taking over forty hours to complete. Group the results by the artisan name to sum the total hours spent on these intricate designs. Sort the final output by the total hours from highest to lowest. Example input: artisan Klaus spending forty five hours on a black forest model. Example output: the name Klaus and the sum of forty five.

);

CREATE TABLE logs (
    log_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    model_id      INTEGER REFERENCES models (model_id),

);

text_es: Write a SQL script `summarize(outages)`. The provided table logs an outage identifier, a station name, and the downtime in hours. A reference table connects the station name to a transit line and a mechanic team. The logic must discard outages shorter than two hours and only consider the red transit line. Link the datasets to count the total number of outages for each mechanic team. Produce a list of the mechanic team and their outage count, sorting the result by the count from highest to lowest. Example input shows a three hour outage at central station on the red line handled by team bravo; output is team bravo and one.

CREATE TABLE outages (

);

text_es: Write a SQL script `evaluate(sculptures)`. The table logs an entry identifier, a block type, and the melt rate in cubic centimeters per hour. A descriptive table pairs the block type with a freezer zone and a judging panel. Eliminate any records where the melt rate is below fifty and the freezer zone is not outdoor. Link the tables to determine the maximum melt rate observed by each judging panel. Return the panel name alongside their maximum melt rate, ordered by the rate from highest to lowest. Example input shows a melt rate of sixty for a block in the outdoor zone judged by panel alpha; output is panel alpha and sixty.
text_nat:
-- evaluate(sculptures): eliminate weak indoor melts, then report each panel's peak melt rate.

CREATE TABLE sculptures (
    entry_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    block_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    melt_rate DECIMAL(8, 2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE block_descriptions (
    block_type VARCHAR(40) PRIMARY KEY,
    freezer_zone VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    judging_panel VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO block_descriptions (block_type, freezer_zone, judging_panel) VALUES
    ('clear_cube', 'outdoor', 'panel alpha'),
    ('frosted_slab', 'indoor', 'panel beta'),
    ('blue_column', 'outdoor', 'panel beta'),
    ('carved_sphere', 'chilled_hall', 'panel gamma');

INSERT INTO sculptures (entry_id, block_type, melt_rate) VALUES
    (1, 'clear_cube', 60.00),
    (2, 'frosted_slab', 42.50),
    (3, 'frosted_slab', 71.00),
    (4, 'blue_column', 38.00),
    (5, 'carved_sphere', 49.99),
    (6, 'carved_sphere', 55.25),
    (7, 'driftwood_ice', 80.00);

-- Entries whose block type is missing from the descriptive table would be lost by the link.
SELECT s.entry_id,
       s.block_type
FROM sculptures AS s
LEFT JOIN block_descriptions AS d
       ON s.block_type = d.block_type
WHERE d.block_type IS NULL
ORDER BY s.entry_id;

-- Elimination step: melt rate below fifty outside of the outdoor zone.
DELETE FROM sculptures
WHERE entry_id IN (
        SELECT s.entry_id
        FROM sculptures AS s
        JOIN block_descriptions AS d
          ON s.block_type = d.block_type
        WHERE s.melt_rate < 50
          AND d.freezer_zone <> 'outdoor'
    );

-- Surviving entries with their zone and panel, for the judges' worksheet.
SELECT s.entry_id,
       d.freezer_zone,
       d.judging_panel,
       s.melt_rate
FROM sculptures AS s
JOIN block_descriptions AS d
  ON s.block_type = d.block_type
ORDER BY d.judging_panel,
         s.melt_rate DESC;

-- Final result: panel name and its maximum melt rate.
SELECT d.judging_panel AS panel_name,
       MAX(s.melt_rate) AS max_melt_rate
FROM sculptures AS s
JOIN block_descriptions AS d
  ON s.block_type = d.block_type
GROUP BY d.judging_panel
ORDER BY MAX(s.melt_rate) DESC;

text_es: Write a SQL script `analyze(tests)`. The input dataset records a test identifier, a lift model, and the tension reading in kilonewtons. A reference dataset pairs the lift model with a mountain peak and an engineer. The query should discard readings below four hundred kilonewtons and only include the summit mountain peak. Connect the datasets to find the lowest tension reading recorded by each engineer. Present the engineer name and their minimum tension reading, ordered from lowest to highest tension. Example input features a four hundred ten kilonewton reading at the summit tested by engineer Patel; output is Patel and four hundred ten.
text_nat:
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS "analyze";
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS summit_readings;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS discarded_readings;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS unmatched_tests;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tests;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS lift_reference;

CREATE TABLE lift_reference (
    lift_model TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    peak       TEXT NOT NULL,
    engineer   TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE tests (
    test_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    lift_model TEXT NOT NULL,
    tension_kn NUMERIC(8,2) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO lift_reference (lift_model, peak, engineer) VALUES
    ('GX-1', 'Summit',    'Patel'),
    ('GX-2', 'Summit',    'Patel'),
    ('HR-7', 'Summit',    'Nakamura'),
    ('LT-3', 'Northface', 'Okoye');

INSERT INTO tests (test_id, lift_model, tension_kn) VALUES
    (1, 'GX-1', 410.00),
    (2, 'GX-2', 455.50),
    (3, 'GX-1', 380.00),
    (4, 'HR-7', 612.25),
    (5, 'HR-7', 499.75),
    (6, 'LT-3', 470.00),
    (7, 'ZZ-9', 520.00);

CREATE VIEW summit_readings AS
SELECT t.test_id,
       r.engineer,
       t.tension_kn
FROM tests
     AS t
JOIN lift_reference
     AS r
     ON t.lift_model = r.lift_model
WHERE t.tension_kn >= 400
  AND r.peak = 'Summit';

CREATE VIEW "analyze" AS
SELECT engineer,
       MIN(tension_kn) AS min_tension_kn
FROM summit_readings
GROUP BY engineer;

CREATE VIEW discarded_readings AS
SELECT t.test_id,
       r.engineer,
       t.tension_kn
FROM tests
     AS t
JOIN lift_reference
     AS r
     ON t.lift_model = r.lift_model
WHERE r.peak = 'Summit'
  AND t.tension_kn < 400;

CREATE VIEW unmatched_tests AS
SELECT t.test_id,
       t.lift_model
FROM tests
     AS t
LEFT JOIN lift_reference
     AS r
     ON t.lift_model = r.lift_model
WHERE r.lift_model IS NULL;

SELECT engineer,
       min_tension_kn
FROM "analyze"
ORDER BY min_tension_kn;

SELECT engineer,
       COUNT(*) AS discarded_count
FROM discarded_readings
GROUP BY engineer
ORDER BY discarded_count DESC;

SELECT test_id,
       lift_model
FROM unmatched_tests
ORDER BY test_id;

text_es: Write a SQL script `summarize(scores)`. The primary table logs a hit identifier, a bumper color, and the points awarded. A secondary table matches the bumper color to a playfield sector and a machine technician. The logic must exclude hits awarding fewer than five hundred points and restrict the sector to the upper playfield. Join the records to total the points awarded under each machine technician. Display the technician name and the total points, sorted from highest to lowest points. Example input has a six hundred point hit in the upper sector maintained by technician Clark; output is Clark and six hundred.
text_nat:
-- Pinball hit summary: total points per machine technician for upper-playfield bumpers.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS scores;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS bumpers;

CREATE TABLE scores (
    hit_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    bumper_color TEXT NOT NULL,
    points       INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE bumpers (
    bumper_color TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    sector       TEXT NOT NULL,
    technician   TEXT NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO bumpers (bumper_color, sector, technician) VALUES
    ('red',    'upper', 'Clark'),
    ('blue',   'upper', 'Diaz'),
    ('green',  'lower', 'Osei'),
    ('yellow', 'upper', 'Clark');

INSERT INTO scores (hit_id, bumper_color, points) VALUES
    (1, 'red',    600),
    (2, 'blue',   450),
    (3, 'green',  900),
    (4, 'yellow', 500),
    (5, 'blue',   750),
    (6, 'purple', 800);

-- Hits that actually count: at least 500 points and scored on the upper playfield.
CREATE VIEW qualifying_hits AS
SELECT s.hit_id AS hit_id,
       b.technician AS technician,
       s.points AS points
FROM scores AS s
JOIN bumpers AS b
ON s.bumper_color = b.bumper_color
WHERE s.points >= 500
AND b.sector = 'upper';

-- summarize(scores): technician name and total qualifying points, highest first.
CREATE VIEW summarize AS
SELECT technician,
       SUM(points) AS total_points
FROM qualifying_hits
GROUP BY technician
ORDER BY total_points DESC;

-- Data check: logged bumper colors that have no entry in the mapping table,
-- so their hits are silently missing from the summary above.
SELECT s.bumper_color AS unmapped_color,
       COUNT(*) AS lost_hits,
       SUM(s.points) AS lost_points
FROM scores AS s
LEFT JOIN bumpers AS b
ON s.bumper_color = b.bumper_color
WHERE b.bumper_color IS NULL
GROUP BY s.bumper_color
ORDER BY lost_points DESC;

-- Driver: the requested summary.
SELECT technician,
       total_points
FROM summarize;

-- Supporting report: each technician's single best qualifying hit,
-- ordered by that technician's overall standing.
SELECT t.technician AS technician,
       q.hit_id AS best_hit,
       q.points AS best_points,
       t.total_points AS total_points
FROM summarize AS t
JOIN qualifying_hits AS q
ON q.technician = t.technician
WHERE q.points = (
        SELECT MAX(m.points)
        FROM qualifying_hits AS m
        WHERE m.technician = t.technician
      )
ORDER BY t.total_points DESC;

text_es: Write a SQL script `calculate(batches)`. The primary table records a batch identifier, an evaporator grade, and the boiling time in hours. A supplementary table links the evaporator grade to a farm region and a quality inspector. Filter the records to include only boiling times greater than eight hours from the northern farm region. Merge the tables to compute the average boiling time overseen by each quality inspector. Return the inspector name and the average time, ordered alphabetically by the inspector name. Example input has a nine hour boil from the northern region inspected by Green; output is Green and nine.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE batches (
    batch_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    evaporator_grade TEXT NOT NULL,
    boiling_hours NUMERIC NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE grade_registry (
    evaporator_grade TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    farm_region TEXT NOT NULL,
    quality_inspector TEXT NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO grade_registry (evaporator_grade, farm_region, quality_inspector) VALUES
    ('AA', 'northern', 'Green'),
    ('AB', 'northern', 'Adams'),
    ('BA', 'southern', 'Miller'),
    ('BB', 'eastern', 'Novak');

INSERT INTO batches (batch_id, evaporator_grade, boiling_hours) VALUES
    (1, 'AA', 9),
    (2, 'AA', 7),
    (3, 'AB', 11),
    (4, 'AB', 13),
    (5, 'BA', 12),
    (6, 'BB', 10),
    (7, 'CC', 14);

CREATE VIEW northern_long_boils AS
SELECT
    b.batch_id,
    b.boiling_hours,
    r.quality_inspector
FROM batches b
JOIN grade_registry r
    ON b.evaporator_grade = r.evaporator_grade
WHERE b.boiling_hours > 8
    AND r.farm_region = 'northern';

CREATE VIEW calculate AS
SELECT
    quality_inspector,
    AVG(boiling_hours) AS average_boiling_hours
FROM northern_long_boils
GROUP BY quality_inspector
ORDER BY quality_inspector;

CREATE VIEW unregistered_grades AS
SELECT DISTINCT
    b.evaporator_grade
FROM batches b
LEFT JOIN grade_registry r
    ON b.evaporator_grade = r.evaporator_grade
WHERE r.evaporator_grade IS NULL;

SELECT
    quality_inspector,
    average_boiling_hours
FROM calculate;

SELECT
    c.quality_inspector,
    ROUND(c.average_boiling_hours, 1) AS mean_hours,
    COUNT(n.batch_id) AS qualifying_batches
FROM calculate c
JOIN northern_long_boils n
    ON n.quality_inspector = c.quality_inspector
GROUP BY c.quality_inspector,
    c.average_boiling_hours
ORDER BY c.quality_inspector;

SELECT evaporator_grade
FROM unregistered_grades
ORDER BY evaporator_grade;

text_es: Formulate a SQL script `calculate(plantations, collections)` to assess latex yields. There is a table of plantations with their identifier and soil type, and a table of collections showing the plantation identifier, liters of sap, and weather condition. Isolate the records where the weather is clear and the soil type is volcanic. Connect the tables using the plantation identifier to find the total liters collected per plantation. Show the plantation name alongside its total sap volume, organized by volume in descending sequence.
text_nat:
-- Latex yield assessment: total sap collected under clear weather on volcanic soil.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS collections;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS plantations;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS plantation_totals;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS qualifying_collections;

CREATE TABLE plantations (
    plantation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    plantation_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    soil_type TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE collections (
    collection_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    plantation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES plantations (plantation_id),
    liters NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    weather TEXT NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO plantations (plantation_id, plantation_name, soil_type) VALUES
    (1, 'Kilauea Grove',   'volcanic'),
    (2, 'Riverbend Rows',  'alluvial'),
    (3, 'Ashfall Terrace', 'volcanic'),
    (4, 'Crater Ridge',    'volcanic'),
    (5, 'Clayfield Stand', 'clay');

INSERT INTO collections (collection_id, plantation_id, liters, weather) VALUES
    (1, 1, 120.5, 'clear'),
    (2, 1,  80.0, 'rain'),
    (3, 1,  95.5, 'clear'),
    (4, 2, 300.0, 'clear'),
    (5, 3, 150.0, 'clear'),
    (6, 3,  40.0, 'overcast'),
    (7, 4,  60.0, 'rain'),
    (8, 5, 210.0, 'clear');

-- Rows that satisfy both conditions: clear weather over volcanic soil.
CREATE VIEW qualifying_collections AS
SELECT
    P.plantation_id,
    P.plantation_name,
    C.liters
FROM
    plantations P
JOIN
    collections C
    ON C.plantation_id = P.plantation_id
WHERE C.weather = 'clear'
    AND P.soil_type = 'volcanic';

-- Aggregated yield per plantation, reusable by the reports below.
CREATE VIEW plantation_totals AS
SELECT
    plantation_id,
    plantation_name,
    SUM(liters) AS total_liters
FROM qualifying_collections
GROUP BY
    plantation_id,
    plantation_name;

-- calculate(plantations, collections): the requested result set.
SELECT
    plantation_name,
    total_liters
FROM plantation_totals
ORDER BY total_liters DESC;

-- Completeness check: volcanic plantations with no clear-weather harvest yet.
SELECT
    P.plantation_name
FROM
    plantations P
LEFT JOIN
    plantation_totals T
    ON T.plantation_id = P.plantation_id
WHERE P.soil_type = 'volcanic'
    AND T.total_liters IS NULL
ORDER BY P.plantation_name;

text_es: Construct `evaluate(vats, tests)` to review soy sauce brewing quality using SQL. You are supplied with a vat table containing the identifier and capacity, and a quality test table with the vat identifier, salt percentage, and umami score. Identify tests where the salt percentage is strictly eighteen percent and the umami score surpasses ninety. Link the tables on the vat identifier to count the number of successful tests per vat. Output the vat identifier and the test count, grouping by the identifier and ordering by the count descending.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE vats (
    vat_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    capacity_liters INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE tests (
    test_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    vat_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    salt_percent DECIMAL(4, 1) NOT NULL,
    umami_score INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO vats (vat_id, capacity_liters) VALUES (1, 4000);
INSERT INTO vats (vat_id, capacity_liters) VALUES (2, 6500);
INSERT INTO vats (vat_id, capacity_liters) VALUES (3, 2500);

INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (101, 1, 18.0, 94);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (102, 1, 18.0, 91);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (103, 1, 17.5, 97);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (104, 2, 18.0, 90);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (105, 2, 18.0, 99);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (106, 3, 18.4, 93);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (107, 3, 18.0, 88);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (108, 4, 18.0, 96);
INSERT INTO tests (test_id, vat_id, salt_percent, umami_score) VALUES (109, 1, 18.0, 150);

DELETE
FROM tests
WHERE umami_score < 0
   OR umami_score > 100;

SELECT
    t.test_id,
    t.vat_id
FROM
    tests AS t
LEFT JOIN
    vats AS v
    ON v.vat_id = t.vat_id
WHERE
    v.vat_id IS NULL
ORDER BY
    t.test_id;

SELECT
    v.vat_id,
    COUNT(t.test_id) AS successful_tests
FROM
    vats AS v
JOIN
    tests AS t
    ON t.vat_id = v.vat_id
WHERE
    t.salt_percent = 18.0
    AND t.umami_score > 90
GROUP BY
    v.vat_id
ORDER BY
    successful_tests DESC;

SELECT
    v.vat_id,
    COUNT(t.test_id) AS total_tests,
    SUM(CASE
            WHEN t.salt_percent = 18.0
            AND t.umami_score > 90
            THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END) AS passed_tests
FROM
    vats AS v
LEFT JOIN
    tests AS t
    ON t.vat_id = v.vat_id
GROUP BY
    v.vat_id
ORDER BY
    passed_tests DESC;

WITH passed AS (
    SELECT
        t.vat_id,
        COUNT(*) AS pass_count
    FROM
        tests AS t
    WHERE
        t.salt_percent = 18.0
        AND t.umami_score > 90
    GROUP BY
        t.vat_id
)
SELECT
    v.vat_id,
    v.capacity_liters,
    p.pass_count,
    RANK() OVER (
        ORDER BY p.pass_count DESC
    ) AS pass_rank
FROM
    vats AS v
JOIN
    passed AS p
    ON p.vat_id = v.vat_id
ORDER BY
    pass_rank;

text_es: Write `grade(farms, harvests)` to evaluate premium wasabi production.
