text_es: Write a SQL-backed function named `align(gates, jumps)`. The gates data includes a gate identifier, a sector name, and a base stability score. The jumps data tracks a jump identifier, the gate identifier, a misalignment angle, and a jump year. Join the two datasets to calculate the average misalignment angle for each sector name. Only consider jumps that occurred after the year three thousand, and only include gates that have a base stability score below fifty. Group the results by sector name and filter to keep only those sectors where the average misalignment angle is strictly greater than ten. Return a list of tuples containing the sector name and the average misalignment angle, ordered by the angle in descending order. Example input: gates with sector Orion and stability forty, jumps with angles twelve and sixteen. Example output: [("Orion", 14)].
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE gates (
    gate_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    sector_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    base_stability INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE jumps (
    jump_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    gate_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    misalignment_angle INTEGER NOT NULL,
    jump_year INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO gates (gate_id, sector_name, base_stability) VALUES
    (1, 'Orion', 40),
    (2, 'Orion', 45),
    (3, 'Lyra', 70),
    (4, 'Draco', 20),
    (5, 'Vega', 35);

INSERT INTO jumps (jump_id, gate_id, misalignment_angle, jump_year) VALUES
    (100, 1, 12, 3010),
    (101, 1, 16, 3025),
    (102, 2, 14, 2990),
    (103, 3, 40, 3100),
    (104, 4, 30, 3050),
    (105, 4, 2, 3051),
    (106, 5, 4, 3060),
    (107, 9, 11, 3070);

CREATE VIEW align AS
SELECT g.sector_name,
       AVG(j.misalignment_angle) AS avg_angle
FROM gates AS g
JOIN jumps AS j
  ON j.gate_id = g.gate_id
WHERE j.jump_year > 3000
  AND g.base_stability < 50
GROUP BY g.sector_name
HAVING AVG(j.misalignment_angle) > 10;

SELECT j.jump_id,
       j.gate_id
FROM jumps AS j
LEFT JOIN gates AS g
  ON g.gate_id = j.gate_id
WHERE g.gate_id IS NULL
ORDER BY j.jump_id;

SELECT g.sector_name,
       g.gate_id,
       COUNT(j.jump_id) AS jump_count,
       MAX(j.misalignment_angle) AS worst_angle,
       CASE
           WHEN MAX(j.misalignment_angle) > 10 THEN 'CRITICAL'
           ELSE 'NOMINAL'
       END AS gate_status
FROM gates AS g
JOIN jumps AS j
  ON j.gate_id = g.gate_id
WHERE g.base_stability < 50
  AND j.jump_year > 3000
GROUP BY g.sector_name,
         g.gate_id
ORDER BY worst_angle DESC;

WITH sector_volume AS (
    SELECT g.sector_name,
           COUNT(*) AS jump_total
    FROM gates AS g
    JOIN jumps AS j
      ON j.gate_id = g.gate_id
    WHERE j.jump_year > 3000
      AND g.base_stability < 50
    GROUP BY g.sector_name
)
SELECT a.sector_name,
       a.avg_angle,
       v.jump_total
FROM align AS a
JOIN sector_volume AS v
  ON v.sector_name = a.sector_name
ORDER BY a.avg_angle DESC;

SELECT sector_name,
       avg_angle
FROM align
ORDER BY avg_angle DESC;

text_es: Implement a SQL-powered function named `armor(suits, battles)`. The suits input provides a suit identifier, a pilot name, and a chassis class. The battles input tracks a battle identifier, the suit identifier, an ablation depth in millimeters, and the number of hits taken. Join the datasets to determine the total ablation depth per pilot name. Restrict the data to heavy chassis class suits and battles where the hits taken were greater than twenty. Group by the pilot name and only include pilots whose total ablation depth is over one hundred millimeters. Return a list of tuples with the pilot name and total ablation depth, sorted by depth descending. Example input: suits piloted by Jax in a heavy chassis, battles with depths of sixty and fifty. Example output: [("Jax", 110)].
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE suits (
    suit_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    pilot_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    chassis_class VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE battles (
    battle_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    suit_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    ablation_depth_mm INTEGER NOT NULL,
    hits_taken INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO suits (suit_id, pilot_name, chassis_class) VALUES
    (1, 'Jax', 'heavy'),
    (2, 'Rill', 'heavy'),
    (3, 'Moya', 'light'),
    (4, 'Doran', 'heavy');

INSERT INTO battles (battle_id, suit_id, ablation_depth_mm, hits_taken) VALUES
    (10, 1, 60, 34),
    (11, 1, 50, 22),
    (12, 1, 90, 12),
    (13, 2, 40, 41),
    (14, 2, 30, 25),
    (15, 3, 200, 55),
    (16, 4, 130, 21);

SELECT s.pilot_name AS pilot_name,
       SUM(b.ablation_depth_mm) AS total_ablation_depth_mm
FROM suits AS s
JOIN battles AS b
    ON s.suit_id = b.suit_id
WHERE s.chassis_class = 'heavy'
  AND b.hits_taken > 20
GROUP BY s.pilot_name
HAVING SUM(b.ablation_depth_mm) > 100
ORDER BY total_ablation_depth_mm DESC;

SELECT s.pilot_name AS pilot_name,
       COUNT(*) AS qualifying_battles,
       MAX(b.ablation_depth_mm) AS worst_battle_depth_mm
FROM suits AS s
JOIN battles AS b
    ON s.suit_id = b.suit_id
WHERE s.chassis_class = 'heavy'
  AND b.hits_taken > 20
GROUP BY s.pilot_name
ORDER BY qualifying_battles DESC;

WITH qualifying AS (
    SELECT s.pilot_name AS pilot_name,
           b.ablation_depth_mm AS depth_mm,
           b.hits_taken AS hits_taken
    FROM suits AS s
    JOIN battles AS b
        ON s.suit_id = b.suit_id
    WHERE s.chassis_class = 'heavy'
      AND b.hits_taken > 20
)
SELECT pilot_name,
       SUM(depth_mm) AS total_ablation_depth_mm,
       CASE
           WHEN SUM(depth_mm) > 100 THEN 'critical'
           ELSE 'serviceable'
       END AS armor_status,
       SUM(depth_mm) / SUM(hits_taken) AS depth_per_hit
FROM qualifying
GROUP BY pilot_name
ORDER BY total_ablation_depth_mm DESC;

UPDATE suits
SET chassis_class = 'heavy-refit'
WHERE suit_id IN (
    SELECT b.suit_id
    FROM battles AS b
    WHERE b.hits_taken > 20
      AND b.ablation_depth_mm > 55
);

DELETE FROM battles
WHERE hits_taken <= 20
  AND ablation_depth_mm < 100;

text_es: Write a function using SQL named `grow(reefs, measurements)`. The reefs data lists a reef identifier, an ocean region, and a coral strain. The measurements data tracks a measurement identifier, the reef identifier, a calcium uptake value, and a water acidity level. Join the lists to sum the total calcium uptake for each ocean region. Consider only reefs growing the luminescent coral strain and measurements where the water acidity level was above eight. Group by ocean region and filter for regions where the total calcium uptake exceeds one thousand units. Return a list of tuples containing the ocean region and total calcium uptake, sorted by uptake in descending order. Example input: reefs in the Pacific region with luminescent strain, measurements showing uptakes of six hundred and five hundred. Example output: [("Pacific", 1100)].
text_nat:
CREATE type reef_row AS (reef_id integer, ocean_region text, coral_strain text);

CREATE type measurement_row AS (
    measurement_id integer,
    reef_id integer,
    calcium_uptake numeric,
    water_acidity numeric
);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION normalized_strain(strain text)
returns text
language sql
immutable
AS $$
    SELECT lower(btrim(strain));
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION grow(reefs reef_row[], measurements measurement_row[])
returns TABLE (ocean_region text, total_calcium_uptake numeric)
language sql
stable
AS $$
    SELECT
        r.ocean_region,
        sum(m.calcium_uptake)
    FROM unnest(reefs)
        AS r
    JOIN unnest(measurements)
        AS m
        ON m.reef_id = r.reef_id
    WHERE normalized_strain(r.coral_strain) = 'luminescent'
      AND m.water_acidity > 8
    GROUP BY r.ocean_region
    HAVING sum(m.calcium_uptake) > 1000
    ORDER BY sum(m.calcium_uptake) DESC;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION reef_contributions(reefs reef_row[], measurements measurement_row[])
returns TABLE (reef_id integer, ocean_region text, reef_uptake numeric)
language sql
stable
AS $$
    SELECT
        r.reef_id,
        r.ocean_region,
        sum(m.calcium_uptake)
    FROM unnest(reefs)
        AS r
    JOIN unnest(measurements)
        AS m
        ON m.reef_id = r.reef_id
    WHERE normalized_strain(r.coral_strain) = 'luminescent'
      AND m.water_acidity > 8
    GROUP BY
        r.reef_id,
        r.ocean_region
    ORDER BY sum(m.calcium_uptake) DESC;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION region_report(reefs reef_row[], measurements measurement_row[])
returns setof text
language sql
stable
AS $$
    SELECT
        g.ocean_region || ': ' || to_char(g.total_calcium_uptake, 'FM999999990.9')
    FROM grow(reefs, measurements)
        AS g
    ORDER BY g.total_calcium_uptake DESC;
$$;

CREATE VIEW sample_survey AS
SELECT
    array[
        row(1, 'Pacific', 'luminescent')::reef_row,
        row(2, 'Pacific', 'Luminescent')::reef_row,
        row(3, 'Atlantic', 'stony')::reef_row
    ] AS reefs,
    array[
        row(1, 1, 600, 8.4)::measurement_row,
        row(2, 2, 500, 8.9)::measurement_row,
        row(3, 1, 900, 7.5)::measurement_row,
        row(4, 3, 4000, 8.6)::measurement_row
    ] AS measurements;

SELECT rep.line
FROM sample_survey
    AS s
CROSS JOIN LATERAL region_report(s.reefs, s.measurements)
    AS rep(line);

SELECT
    c.reef_id,
    c.ocean_region,
    c.reef_uptake
FROM sample_survey
    AS s
CROSS JOIN LATERAL reef_contributions(s.reefs, s.measurements)
    AS c
JOIN grow(s.reefs, s.measurements)
    AS g
    ON g.ocean_region = c.ocean_region
ORDER BY c.reef_uptake DESC;

text_es: Implement a function utilizing SQL named `empathize(androids, behaviors)`. The androids table has an android identifier, an occupation role, and a matrix version. The behaviors table tracks a behavior identifier, the android identifier, an empathy score, and an anomaly flag. Join the tables to calculate the average empathy score for each occupation role. Filter for androids running matrix version three and behaviors where the anomaly flag is set to true. Group by occupation role and retain only roles where the average empathy score is strictly less than fifty. Return a list of tuples containing the occupation role and average empathy score, ordered ascending by the empathy score. Example input: androids in a Medic role on version three, behaviors with anomaly flags and empathy scores of forty and forty-six. Example output: [("Medic", 43)].
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE androids (
    android_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    occupation_role VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    matrix_version INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE behaviors (
    behavior_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    android_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    empathy_score INTEGER NOT NULL,
    anomaly_flag BOOLEAN NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO androids (android_id, occupation_role, matrix_version) VALUES
    (1, 'Medic', 3),
    (2, 'Medic', 3),
    (3, 'Pilot', 3),
    (4, 'Miner', 2);

INSERT INTO behaviors (behavior_id, android_id, empathy_score, anomaly_flag) VALUES
    (10, 1, 40, TRUE),
    (11, 2, 46, TRUE),
    (12, 2, 88, FALSE),
    (13, 3, 71, TRUE),
    (14, 4, 12, TRUE),
    (15, 9, 20, TRUE);

DELETE FROM behaviors
WHERE android_id NOT IN (SELECT android_id FROM androids);

CREATE VIEW empathize AS
SELECT a.occupation_role,
       AVG(b.empathy_score) AS average_empathy
FROM androids AS a
JOIN behaviors AS b
  ON b.android_id = a.android_id
WHERE a.matrix_version = 3
  AND b.anomaly_flag = TRUE
GROUP BY a.occupation_role
HAVING AVG(b.empathy_score) < 50;

SELECT occupation_role,
       average_empathy
FROM empathize
ORDER BY average_empathy;

SELECT e.occupation_role,
       e.average_empathy,
       COUNT(b.behavior_id) AS anomaly_count,
       MIN(b.empathy_score) AS lowest_score
FROM empathize AS e
JOIN androids AS a
  ON a.occupation_role = e.occupation_role
JOIN behaviors AS b
  ON b.android_id = a.android_id
WHERE a.matrix_version = 3
  AND b.anomaly_flag = TRUE
GROUP BY e.occupation_role,
         e.average_empathy
ORDER BY anomaly_count DESC;

WITH flagged AS (
    SELECT a.android_id,
           a.occupation_role,
           b.empathy_score
    FROM androids AS a
    JOIN behaviors AS b
      ON b.android_id = a.android_id
    WHERE a.matrix_version = 3
      AND b.anomaly_flag = TRUE
)
SELECT f.android_id,
       f.occupation_role,
       f.empathy_score,
       CASE
           WHEN f.empathy_score < 45 THEN 'recall'
           ELSE 'monitor'
       END AS disposition
FROM flagged AS f
JOIN empathize AS e
  ON e.occupation_role = f.occupation_role
ORDER BY f.empathy_score,
         f.android_id;

text_es: Write a SQL script containing a helper view to filter routines with a difficulty above five, and a main procedure `evaluate(season)` for synchronized swimming data. The database holds a table of teams with their country and coach, and a table of routines with the team, formation difficulty, execution score, and penalty points. The main procedure must use these tables to return the country and total final score for each team in the given season, calculated as difficulty plus execution minus penalties, ordered from highest to lowest score. It must also return a second query identifying coaches whose teams average an execution score below seven and have exactly zero penalties. Example: input 2023 with a team from France scoring 8 difficulty and 9 execution with 0 penalties returns France with 17 points.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE teams (
  team_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  country VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
  coach VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE routines (
  routine_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  team_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES teams (team_id),
  season INTEGER NOT NULL,
  formation_difficulty DECIMAL(4, 2) NOT NULL,
  execution_score DECIMAL(4, 2) NOT NULL,
  penalty_points DECIMAL(4, 2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW hard_routines
  AS
SELECT routine_id,
       team_id,
       season,
       formation_difficulty,
       execution_score,
       penalty_points
FROM routines
WHERE formation_difficulty > 5;

INSERT INTO teams (team_id, country, coach) VALUES
  (1, 'France', 'Claire Dubois'),
  (2, 'Japan', 'Aiko Tanaka'),
  (3, 'Spain', 'Marta Ruiz'),
  (4, 'Canada', 'Erin Blake');

INSERT INTO routines (routine_id, team_id, season, formation_difficulty, execution_score, penalty_points) VALUES
  (1, 1, 2023, 8.00, 9.00, 0.00),
  (2, 2, 2023, 7.50, 8.00, 0.50),
  (3, 3, 2023, 6.00, 6.50, 0.00),
  (4, 3, 2023, 5.50, 6.20, 0.00),
  (5, 4, 2023, 4.50, 8.00, 0.00),
  (6, 1, 2022, 7.00, 8.50, 1.00);

CREATE PROCEDURE evaluate(IN season INTEGER)
BEGIN
  SELECT t.country,
         SUM(r.formation_difficulty + r.execution_score - r.penalty_points)
           AS final_score
  FROM teams t
  JOIN routines r
    ON r.team_id = t.team_id
  WHERE r.season = season
  GROUP BY t.team_id,
           t.country
  ORDER BY final_score DESC;

  SELECT t.coach,
         t.country,
         AVG(r.execution_score)
           AS average_execution
  FROM teams t
  JOIN routines r
    ON r.team_id = t.team_id
  WHERE r.season = season
  GROUP BY t.team_id,
           t.coach,
           t.country
  HAVING AVG(r.execution_score) < 7
     AND SUM(r.penalty_points) = 0
  ORDER BY average_execution;

  SELECT t.country,
         COUNT(h.routine_id)
           AS hard_routine_count
  FROM teams t
  JOIN hard_routines h
    ON h.team_id = t.team_id
  WHERE h.season = season
  GROUP BY t.team_id,
           t.country
  ORDER BY hard_routine_count DESC;
END;

CALL evaluate(2023);

text_es: Write a SQL script with a helper view to isolate coastal zones deeper than one hundred meters, and a main procedure `monitor(region)` for tracking algae blooms. There is a table of coastal zones with their name and water depth, and a table of bloom events storing the zone, glow intensity, water temperature, and nutrient concentration. The main procedure must combine the tables to return the zone name and the maximum glow intensity for the specified region, looking only at events where water temperature is below twenty degrees and nutrient concentration is above fifty, sorted by highest intensity. It must also provide a list of zones that have an average nutrient concentration below thirty and a glow intensity of exactly zero. Example: region North with a zone of 15 degrees, 60 nutrients, and 80 glow returns North zone with 80 maximum intensity.

CREATE TABLE coastal_zones (

    zone_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,

    water_depth DECIMAL(7, 2) NOT NULL
);

);

CREATE VIEW deep_coastal_zones AS

The database maintains a table of dogs with their name and breed, and a table of race segments tracking the dog, position in the team, pulling force, and segment distance. The procedure should analyze the given race to return the breed and total distance pulled for dogs in the lead position, filtering for segments where the pulling force is at least fifty, grouped by breed and ordered by highest total distance. Additionally, it must output the names of dogs who pulled less than twenty force in the wheel position and have a breed of Husky. Example: race 3 with a Husky in lead pulling 60 force for 15 distance returns Husky with 15 total distance.

Write a SQL script providing a helper view to filter buggies with slick tires, and a main procedure `measure(tournament)` for kite buggy races. The system uses a table of buggies with their model and tire type, and a table of race logs recording the buggy, wind speed, traction coefficient, and wheel sinkage. The main procedure should join the tables to output the tire type and average traction coefficient for the given tournament, only including logs where wind speed is between fifteen and twenty five and wheel sinkage is below five, ordered by the highest average traction. It also needs to list buggy models that achieved a perfect traction coefficient of one while experiencing wind speeds above thirty. Example: tournament 2 with a slick tire buggy at 20 wind speed and 0.8 traction returns slick tire with 0.8 average traction.

Write a SQL script creating a helper view for instruments made of maple wood, and a procedure `evaluate(session)` for instrument maintenance records. The records consist of a table of instruments with their serial number and wood type, and a table of maintenance logs containing the instrument, wheel speed, rosin type, and friction resistance. The procedure must join these tables for the given session to return the wood type and the count of logs where rosin type is dark and wheel speed exceeds one hundred, grouped by wood type and sorted by the highest count. It should also output the serial numbers of instruments that used light rosin and achieved a friction resistance of exactly zero. Write a SQL script featuring a helper view to identify non-fiction reading attempts, and a main procedure `score(competition)` for speed reading events. The data includes a table of readers with their name and age group, and a table of reading attempts detailing the reader, book genre, words per minute, and quiz score. The procedure must join the tables for a specific competition to return the age group and average quiz score, filtering for attempts where words per minute is above five hundred, grouped by age group and ordered by highest average score. It must also list the names of readers who scored a perfect one hundred on the quiz while reading fiction books at over three hundred words per minute. Example: competition 1 with a teen reader at 600 words per minute and 90 score returns the teen group with a 90 average.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE readers (
  reader_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  reader_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
  age_group VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE reading_attempts (
  attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  competition_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reader_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  book_genre VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  words_per_minute INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quiz_score INTEGER NOT NULL
);

  (4, 'Peter Vane', 'adult');

  (1, 1, 1, 'fiction', 600, 90),
  (2, 1, 2, 'history', 540, 75),
  (3, 1, 3, 'fiction', 320, 100),
  (4, 1, 4, 'fiction', 480, 100),
  (5, 2, 1, 'biography', 610, 60);

CREATE VIEW non_fiction_attempts
AS
SELECT
  a.attempt_id,
  a.competition_id,
  a.reader_id,
  a.words_per_minute,
  a.quiz_score
FROM
  reading_attempts AS a
WHERE
  a.book_genre <> 'fiction';

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE score(IN competition INTEGER)
BEGIN
  SELECT
    r.age_group,
    AVG(a.quiz_score) AS average_quiz_score
  FROM
    readers AS r
  JOIN
    reading_attempts AS a
  ON
    a.reader_id = r.reader_id
  WHERE
    a.competition_id = competition
    AND a.words_per_minute > 500
  GROUP BY
    r.age_group
  ORDER BY
    average_quiz_score DESC;

  SELECT
    r.reader_name
  FROM
    readers AS r
  JOIN
    reading_attempts AS a
  ON
    a.reader_id = r.reader_id
  WHERE
    a.competition_id = competition
    AND a.book_genre = 'fiction'
    AND a.words_per_minute > 300
    AND a.quiz_score = 100
  ORDER BY
    r.reader_name;

  SELECT
    r.age_group,
    COUNT(*) AS non_fiction_count,
    AVG(n.words_per_minute) AS average_speed
  FROM
    readers AS r
  JOIN
    non_fiction_attempts AS n
  ON
    n.reader_id = r.reader_id
  WHERE
    n.competition_id = competition
  GROUP BY
    r.age_group
  ORDER BY
    average_speed DESC;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL score(1);

text_es: Write a SQL script containing a helper view to select recordings above ninety decibels, and a procedure `calculate(festival)` for yodeling acoustic data. The schema features a table of yodelers with their name and vocal range, and a table of echo recordings storing the yodeler, canyon location, decibel level, and echo delay in seconds. The procedure should process the given festival to return the canyon location and the maximum echo delay, focusing on recordings where the vocal range is falsetto, grouped by canyon and ordered by longest delay. Furthermore, it must return the names of yodelers who produced an echo delay of exactly five seconds at the Grand Canyon with a baritone vocal range. Example: festival 4 with a falsetto yodel at 95 decibels producing a 3 second delay at Echo Peak returns Echo Peak with a 3 second maximum delay.
text_nat:
-- Acoustic data model for a yodeling festival.
CREATE TABLE yodelers (
    yodeler_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    yodeler_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    vocal_range VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE echo_recordings (
    recording_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    festival_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    yodeler_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES yodelers (yodeler_id),
    canyon_location VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    decibel_level INTEGER NOT NULL,
    echo_delay_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (2, 4, 3, 'Echo Peak', 92, 2);

INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (4, 4, 2, 'Grand Canyon', 97, 5);
INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (5, 4, 4, 'Grand Canyon', 91, 5);
INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (6, 4, 4, 'Grand Canyon', 99, 4);
INSERT INTO echo_recordings VALUES (7, 5, 1, 'Echo Peak', 96, 9);

-- Helper view: only recordings louder than ninety decibels are usable.
CREATE VIEW loud_recordings AS
SELECT
    r.recording_id,
    r.festival_id,
    r.yodeler_id,
    r.canyon_location,
    r.decibel_level,
    r.echo_delay_seconds
FROM
    echo_recordings AS r
WHERE
    r.decibel_level > 90;

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE calculate(IN festival INTEGER)
BEGIN
    -- Longest falsetto echo per canyon for the requested festival.
    SELECT
        lr.canyon_location,
        MAX(lr.echo_delay_seconds) AS max_echo_delay
    FROM
        loud_recordings AS lr
    JOIN
        yodelers AS y
    ON
        lr.yodeler_id = y.yodeler_id
    WHERE
        lr.festival_id = festival
    AND
        y.vocal_range = 'falsetto'
    GROUP BY
        lr.canyon_location
    ORDER BY
        max_echo_delay DESC;

    -- Baritones with a five second Grand Canyon echo.
    SELECT
        y.yodeler_name,
        lr.canyon_location,
        lr.echo_delay_seconds
    FROM
        loud_recordings AS lr
    JOIN
        yodelers AS y
    ON
        y.yodeler_id = lr.yodeler_id
    WHERE
        lr.festival_id = festival
    AND
        y.vocal_range = 'baritone'
    AND
        lr.canyon_location = 'Grand Canyon'
    AND
        lr.echo_delay_seconds = 5
    ORDER BY
        y.yodeler_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL calculate(4);

text_es: Write a SQL script with a helper view to filter shifts on highly complex chords, and a procedure `analyze(recital)` for guitar performance metrics. The database holds a table of guitarists with their name and experience level, and a table of chord shifts tracking the guitarist, song name, chord complexity, and transition time in milliseconds. The procedure must join the tables for a specific recital to return the experience level and the average transition time, including only shifts where the song name is Girl from Ipanema, grouped by experience level and ordered by fastest average time. It should also output the names of guitarists who achieved a transition time of under fifty milliseconds on medium complexity chords. Example: recital 9 with a veteran guitarist transitioning in 120 milliseconds on high complexity returns the veteran level with a 120 average time.
text_nat:
-- Guitar performance metrics: schema, a helper view for highly complex chords,
-- and the analyze(recital) procedure that reports the two result sets.

CREATE TABLE guitarists (
    guitarist_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    experience_level VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE chord_shifts (
    shift_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    recital_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    guitarist_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    song_name VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    chord_complexity VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    transition_ms INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW complex_chord_shifts AS
SELECT s.shift_id,
       s.recital_id,
       s.song_name,
       s.transition_ms,
       g.name AS guitarist_name,
       g.experience_level
FROM chord_shifts s
    JOIN guitarists g
        ON g.guitarist_id = s.guitarist_id
WHERE s.chord_complexity = 'high';

    (3, 9, 2, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'high', 210),
    (4, 9, 3, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'medium', 78),
    (5, 9, 4, 'Wave', 'high', 95),
    (6, 9, 4, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'medium', 38),
    (7, 11, 1, 'Girl from Ipanema', 'high', 150);

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE analyze(IN recital INTEGER)
BEGIN
    SELECT experience_level,
           AVG(transition_ms) AS avg_transition_ms
    FROM complex_chord_shifts
    WHERE recital_id = recital
        AND song_name = 'Girl from Ipanema'
    GROUP BY experience_level
    ORDER BY avg_transition_ms;

    SELECT DISTINCT g.name AS guitarist_name
    FROM chord_shifts s
        JOIN guitarists g
            ON g.guitarist_id = s.guitarist_id
    WHERE s.recital_id = recital
        AND s.chord_complexity = 'medium'
        AND s.transition_ms < 50
    ORDER BY guitarist_name;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL analyze(9);

Schema: Products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL), Inventory (product_id INT, quantity INT, last_updated DATE).

Queries:
1. List all products and their current quantities.
2. Find products in a specific category (e.g., 'Electronics').
3. Calculate the total value of inventory for all products (price * quantity).
4. Add a new product.
5. Update the quantity of an existing product.

    P.price,
    I.quantity
FROM

JOIN

    name,
    price,
    quantity
FROM
    Products

    Inventory ON Products.product_id = Inventory.product_id

    category = 'Electronics';

FROM
    Products AS P

    Inventory AS I ON P.product_id = I.product_id;

Schema: Posts (post_id INT, title VARCHAR, content TEXT, publish_date DATE), Categories (category_id INT, category_name VARCHAR), PostCategories (post_id INT, category_id INT).

Queries:
1. List all posts and their categories.
2. Find all posts belonging to a specific category (e.g., 'Technology').
3. Count the number of posts per category.
4. Create a new blog post.
5. Add a category to an existing post.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all posts and their categories.
SELECT
    P.post_id,
    P.title,
    P.publish_date,
    C.category_name
FROM
    Posts AS P
JOIN
    PostCategories AS PC ON P.post_id = PC.post_id
JOIN
    Categories AS C ON PC.category_id = C.category_id
ORDER BY
    P.publish_date DESC, P.post_id;

-- 2. Find all posts belonging to a specific category (e.g., 'Technology').
SELECT
    P.post_id,
    P.title,
    P.publish_date
FROM
    Posts AS P
JOIN
    PostCategories AS PC ON P.post_id = PC.post_id
JOIN
    Categories AS C ON PC.category_id = C.category_id
WHERE
    C.category_name = 'Technology'
ORDER BY
    P.publish_date DESC;

-- 3. Count the number of posts per category.
SELECT
    C.category_name,
    COUNT(PC.post_id) AS post_count
FROM
    Categories AS C
LEFT JOIN
    PostCategories AS PC ON C.category_id = PC.category_id
GROUP BY
    C.category_name
ORDER BY
    post_count DESC;

Queries:
1. Select all players and their highest scores in any game.
2. Find all scores for a specific game (e.g., 'Space Invaders').
3. Calculate the average score for each player.
4. Add a new player.
5. Record a new game score.
text_nat:

    P.username,

FROM

    Scores S ON P.player_id = S.player_id
GROUP BY
    P.username;

    P.username,

FROM

JOIN

JOIN
    Games G ON S.game_id = G.game_id
WHERE
    G.game_name = 'Space Invaders'
ORDER BY
    S.score DESC;

SELECT
    P.username,

FROM
    Players P
JOIN
    Scores S ON P.player_id = S.player_id
GROUP BY
    P.username;

1. List all tickets and the customers who opened them.
2. Find all 'Open' tickets assigned to a specific agent (e.g., 'John Doe').
3. Count the number of tickets per status.
4. Create a new support ticket.
5. Update a ticket's status to 'Resolved'.
text_nat:
SELECT
  T.ticket_id,
  T.subject,
  C.name AS customer_name,
  C.email AS customer_email
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Customers AS C
  ON T.customer_id = C.customer_id;

SELECT
  T.ticket_id,
  T.subject,
  T.description,
  T.assigned_to
FROM Tickets AS T
WHERE
  T.status = 'Open' AND T.assigned_to = 'John Doe';

SELECT
  status,
  COUNT(ticket_id) AS ticket_count
FROM Tickets
GROUP BY
  status;

Schema: Projects (project_id INT, project_name VARCHAR, start_date DATE, end_date DATE), Milestones (milestone_id INT, project_id INT, milestone_name VARCHAR, due_date DATE, completion_date DATE, status VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. Select all milestones for a specific project (e.g., project_id = 10).
2. Find all 'Overdue' milestones.
3. Count the number of completed milestones per project.
4. Add a new milestone to a project.
5. Update a milestone's status to 'Completed' and set completion date.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Milestones
WHERE project_id = 10;

SELECT milestone_name, due_date
FROM Milestones
WHERE status = 'Pending' AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE;

SELECT p.project_name, COUNT(m.milestone_id) AS completed_milestones_count
FROM Projects p
JOIN Milestones m ON p.project_id = m.project_id
WHERE m.status = 'Completed'
GROUP BY p.project_name
ORDER BY completed_milestones_count DESC;

INSERT INTO Milestones (project_id, milestone_name, due_date, status)
VALUES (10, 'Final Review', '2024-12-31', 'Pending');

UPDATE Milestones
SET status = 'Completed', completion_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE milestone_id = 5;

SELECT P.project_name, M.milestone_name, M.due_date, M.status
FROM Projects P
JOIN Milestones M ON P.project_id = M.project_id
WHERE P.project_name = 'Alpha Project'
ORDER BY M.due_date ASC;

DELETE FROM Milestones
WHERE status = 'Cancelled';

Schema: Campaigns (campaign_id INT, campaign_name VARCHAR, start_date DATE, end_date DATE, budget DECIMAL), Channels (channel_id INT, channel_name VARCHAR, channel_type VARCHAR), Performance (performance_id INT, campaign_id INT, channel_id INT, date DATE, impressions INT, clicks INT, conversions INT).

Queries:
1. List all campaigns and their performance metrics.
2. Find performance data for a specific campaign (e.g., 'Summer Sale').
3. Calculate the total clicks for each channel type.
4. Add a new marketing campaign.
5. Record new performance data for a campaign and channel.
text_nat:
SELECT
  c.campaign_id,
  c.campaign_name,
  c.start_date,
  c.end_date,
  c.budget,
  p.date AS performance_date,
  p.impressions,
  p.clicks,
  p.conversions
FROM
  Campaigns AS c
JOIN
  Performance AS p ON c.campaign_id = p.campaign_id;

SELECT
  p.date,
  p.impressions,
  p.clicks,
  p.conversions,
  ch.channel_name
FROM
  Performance AS p
JOIN
  Campaigns AS c ON p.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
JOIN
  Channels AS ch ON p.channel_id = ch.channel_id
WHERE
  c.campaign_name = 'Summer Sale';

SELECT
  ch.channel_type,
  SUM(p.clicks) AS total_clicks
FROM
  Channels AS ch
JOIN
  Performance AS p ON ch.channel_id = p.channel_id
GROUP BY
  ch.channel_type;

Queries:
1. Select all referrals and the names of the referring and referred providers.
2. Find all patients referred by a specific provider (e.g., referring_provider_id = 1).
3. Count the number of referrals per specialty.
4. Add a new healthcare provider.

SELECT
  R.referral_id,
  P.first_name,
  P.last_name,
  RP.provider_name AS referring_provider_name,
  TP.provider_name AS referred_provider_name,
  R.referral_date,
  R.reason
FROM Referrals AS R
JOIN Patients AS P
  ON R.patient_id = P.patient_id
JOIN Providers AS RP
  ON R.referring_provider_id = RP.provider_id
JOIN Providers AS TP
  ON R.referred_provider_id = TP.provider_id;

SELECT
  P.first_name,
  P.last_name
FROM Patients AS P
JOIN Referrals AS R
  ON P.patient_id = R.patient_id
WHERE
  R.referring_provider_id = 1;

SELECT
  PV.specialty,
  COUNT(R.referral_id) AS referral_count
FROM Referrals AS R
JOIN Providers AS PV
  ON R.referred_provider_id = PV.provider_id
GROUP BY
  PV.specialty;

FROM
    Users AS U
LEFT JOIN
    Albums AS A ON U.user_id = A.user_id

    Photos AS P ON A.album_id = P.album_id
GROUP BY
    U.username
ORDER BY

SELECT

    D.donation_amount,
    D.donation_date,
    DN.first_name,
    DN.last_name,
    C.campaign_name

    Donations AS D

    Departments d

Queries:

2. Find all episodes from a specific podcast (e.g., 'Daily News Digest').

SELECT
    E.episode_id,
    E.episode_title,
    P.podcast_title,
    P.host
FROM
    Episodes AS E
JOIN
    Podcasts AS P

Queries:
1. List all students enrolled in 'Calculus I' who received an 'A'.
2. Calculate the total credits each student is currently taking.
3. Find the average grade for each course.
4. Enroll a new student in two specific courses.
5. Update a student's major and their grade in a course.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Students (StudentID, FirstName, LastName, Major) VALUES
(1, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'Math'),
(2, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'Physics'),
(3, 'Charlie', 'Brown', 'Math');

(102, 'Physics I', 4),
(103, 'Linear Algebra', 3);

(1002, 1, 103, 'B'),
(1003, 2, 102, 'A'),
(1004, 3, 101, 'B');

-- 1. List all students enrolled in 'Calculus I' who received an 'A'.
SELECT S.FirstName, S.LastName
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.StudentID = E.StudentID
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.CourseID = C.CourseID
WHERE C.CourseName = 'Calculus I' AND E.Grade = 'A';

-- 2. Calculate the total credits each student is currently taking.
SELECT S.FirstName, S.LastName, SUM(C.Credits) AS TotalCredits
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.StudentID = E.StudentID
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.CourseID = C.CourseID
GROUP BY S.StudentID, S.FirstName, S.LastName;

-- 3. Find the average grade for each course. (Assuming A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0)
SELECT C.CourseName, AVG(CASE E.Grade
    WHEN 'A' THEN 4
    WHEN 'B' THEN 3
    WHEN 'C' THEN 2
    WHEN 'D' THEN 1
    ELSE 0 END) AS AverageGrade
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.CourseID = E.CourseID
GROUP BY C.CourseName;

Queries:
1. Find all books currently overdue (ReturnDate is NULL and BorrowDate is more than 30 days ago).
2. List the number of books borrowed by each borrower.
3. Identify books written by 'Jane Austen' that are currently available.
4. Record a new book loan for an existing borrower.

text_nat:
-- 1. Find all books currently overdue
SELECT
    B.Title,
    B.Author
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN
    Loans AS L ON B.BookID = L.BookID
WHERE
    L.ReturnDate IS NULL
    AND L.BorrowDate < DATE('now', '-30 days');

-- 2. List the number of books borrowed by each borrower
SELECT
    BR.Name,
    COUNT(L.LoanID) AS NumberOfBooksBorrowed
FROM
    Borrowers AS BR
LEFT JOIN
    Loans AS L ON BR.BorrowerID = L.BorrowerID
GROUP BY
    BR.Name
ORDER BY
    NumberOfBooksBorrowed DESC;

-- 3. Identify books written by 'Jane Austen' that are currently available
SELECT
    Title
FROM
    Books
WHERE
    Author = 'Jane Austen'
    AND AvailableCopies > 0;

-- 4. Record a new book loan for an existing borrower

VALUES (101, 201, DATE('now'), NULL);

UPDATE Books
SET AvailableCopies = AvailableCopies - 1
WHERE BookID = 101;

UPDATE Loans
SET ReturnDate = DATE('now')
WHERE LoanID = 501;

UPDATE Books
SET AvailableCopies = AvailableCopies + 1
WHERE BookID = (SELECT BookID FROM Loans WHERE LoanID = 501);

    COUNT(b.BugID) > 10;

Queries:
1. List all players on the 'Lions' team who play 'Forward'.
2. Calculate the total wins for each team.
3. Find teams that have played more than 10 games.
4. Add a new player to an existing team.
5. Update the score of a specific game.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Players (PlayerID, FirstName, LastName, TeamID, Position)

UPDATE Games
SET HomeScore = 3, AwayScore = 1
WHERE GameID = 5;

  P.FirstName,
  P.LastName
FROM Players AS P
JOIN Teams AS T
  ON P.TeamID = T.TeamID
WHERE
  T.TeamName = 'Lions' AND P.Position = 'Forward';

SELECT
  T.TeamName,
  SUM(CASE
    WHEN G.HomeTeamID = T.TeamID AND G.HomeScore > G.AwayScore THEN 1
    WHEN G.AwayTeamID = T.TeamID AND G.AwayScore > G.HomeScore THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END) AS TotalWins
FROM Teams AS T
LEFT JOIN Games AS G
  ON T.TeamID = G.HomeTeamID OR T.TeamID = G.AwayTeamID
GROUP BY
  T.TeamName
ORDER BY
  TotalWins DESC;

SELECT
  T.TeamName,
  COUNT(G.GameID) AS GamesPlayed
FROM Teams AS T
JOIN Games AS G
  ON T.TeamID = G.HomeTeamID OR T.TeamID = G.AwayTeamID
GROUP BY
  T.TeamName
HAVING
  COUNT(G.GameID) > 10;

Schema: Rooms(RoomID INT, RoomNumber VARCHAR(10), RoomType VARCHAR(50), PricePerNight DECIMAL(8,2)), Guests(GuestID INT, FirstName VARCHAR(50), LastName VARCHAR(50), Email VARCHAR(100)), Reservations(ReservationID INT, RoomID INT, GuestID INT, CheckInDate DATE, CheckOutDate DATE, TotalPrice DECIMAL(10,2)).
Queries:
1. List all available 'Suite' rooms for a specific date range.
2. Calculate the total revenue generated by each room type.
3. Find guests who have made more than 3 reservations.
4. Make a new reservation for a guest in a specific room.
5. Update the check-out date of an existing reservation and adjust the total price.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all available 'Suite' rooms for a specific date range.
SELECT
    R.RoomNumber,
    R.PricePerNight
FROM
    Rooms AS R
WHERE
    R.RoomType = 'Suite'
    AND R.RoomID NOT IN (
        SELECT
            RES.RoomID
        FROM
            Reservations AS RES
        WHERE
            (RES.CheckInDate < '2023-11-20' AND RES.CheckOutDate > '2023-11-15')
    );

-- 2. Calculate the total revenue generated by each room type.
SELECT
    R.RoomType,
    SUM(RES.TotalPrice) AS TotalRevenue
FROM
    Rooms AS R
JOIN
    Reservations AS RES ON R.RoomID = RES.RoomID
GROUP BY
    R.RoomType;

-- 3. Find guests who have made more than 3 reservations.
SELECT
    G.FirstName,
    G.LastName,
    COUNT(RES.ReservationID) AS NumberOfReservations
FROM
    Guests AS G
JOIN
    Reservations AS RES ON G.GuestID = RES.GuestID
GROUP BY
    G.GuestID, G.FirstName, G.LastName
HAVING
    COUNT(RES.ReservationID) > 3;

-- 4. Make a new reservation for a guest in a specific room.
INSERT INTO Reservations (RoomID, GuestID, CheckInDate, CheckOutDate, TotalPrice)
VALUES (101, 201, '2023-12-01', '2023-12-05', 400.00);

-- 5. Update the check-out date of an existing reservation and adjust the total price.
UPDATE Reservations
SET
    CheckOutDate = '2023-12-07',
    TotalPrice = (SELECT PricePerNight FROM Rooms WHERE RoomID = Reservations.RoomID) * DATEDIFF('2023-12-07', CheckInDate)
WHERE
    ReservationID = 1;

Queries:
1. List all 'In Progress' modules for 'User A' in 'Introduction to SQL'.
2. Calculate the percentage of modules completed by each user in a specific course.
3. Find courses where all enrolled students have completed at least 50% of the modules.
4. Enroll a new user in a course and mark the first module as 'Completed'.
5. Update the 'CompletionStatus' of a module for a user.

UPDATE Progress
SET CompletionStatus = 'Completed', CompletionDate = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE EnrollmentID = 100 AND ModuleID = 202;

SELECT DISTINCT M.ModuleName
FROM Courses C
JOIN Modules M ON C.CourseID = M.CourseID
JOIN Enrollments E ON C.CourseID = E.CourseID
JOIN Progress P ON E.EnrollmentID = P.EnrollmentID AND M.ModuleID = P.ModuleID
WHERE C.CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL'
  AND E.UserID = (SELECT UserID FROM Users WHERE UserName = 'User A')
  AND P.CompletionStatus = 'In Progress';

SELECT U.UserName, (COUNT(CASE WHEN P.CompletionStatus = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT M.ModuleID)) AS CompletionPercentage
FROM Users U
JOIN Enrollments E ON U.UserID = E.UserID
JOIN Courses C ON E.CourseID = C.CourseID
JOIN Modules M ON C.CourseID = M.CourseID
LEFT JOIN Progress P ON E.EnrollmentID = P.EnrollmentID AND M.ModuleID = P.ModuleID
WHERE C.CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL'
GROUP BY U.UserName;

SELECT C.CourseName
FROM Courses C
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT E.UserID
    FROM Enrollments E
    WHERE E.CourseID = C.CourseID
    GROUP BY E.UserID
    HAVING (COUNT(CASE WHEN P.CompletionStatus = 'Completed' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT M.ModuleID)) < 50
);

    P.PostContent,
    P.PostDate
FROM
    Posts AS P
JOIN
    Users AS U ON P.UserID = U.UserID
WHERE

AND
    P.PostID IN (
        SELECT
            PostID
        FROM
            Likes

    COUNT(L.LikeID) AS TotalLikes

GROUP BY

ORDER BY

JOIN
    Posts AS P ON U.UserID = P.UserID
GROUP BY

    COUNT(P.PostID) > 20

FROM Members

SELECT m.FirstName, m.LastName, COUNT(l.BookID) AS BooksOnLoan

text_es: Schema: Documents (doc_id, title, latest_version_id), Versions (version_id, doc_id, version_number, content, created_at, created_by). Queries: 1. Retrieve the latest content for a specific document. 2. Find all versions of a document, ordered by version number. 3. Insert a new version for an existing document, updating the latest_version_id in Documents. 4. Find all documents created by a specific user. 5. Get the count of versions for each document.
text_nat:
-- 1. Retrieve the latest content for a specific document
SELECT
    v.content
FROM
    Documents d
JOIN
    Versions v ON d.latest_version_id = v.version_id
WHERE
    d.doc_id = 1; -- Replace 1 with the desired doc_id

-- 2. Find all versions of a document, ordered by version number
SELECT
    version_id,
    version_number,
    content,
    created_at,
    created_by
FROM
    Versions
WHERE
    doc_id = 2 -- Replace 2 with the desired doc_id
ORDER BY
    version_number ASC;

-- 3. Insert a new version for an existing document, updating the latest_version_id in Documents
-- First, insert the new version
INSERT INTO Versions (doc_id, version_number, content, created_at, created_by)
VALUES (3, (SELECT MAX(version_number) + 1 FROM Versions WHERE doc_id = 3), 'New content for doc 3', NOW(), 'user_A');

-- Then, update the Documents table
UPDATE Documents
SET latest_version_id = (SELECT version_id FROM Versions WHERE doc_id = 3 ORDER BY version_number DESC LIMIT 1)
WHERE doc_id = 3;

-- 4. Find all documents created by a specific user
SELECT
    DISTINCT d.doc_id,
    d.title
FROM
    Documents d
JOIN
    Versions v ON d.doc_id = v.doc_id
WHERE
    v.created_by = 'user_B'; -- Replace 'user_B' with the desired username

-- 5. Get the count of versions for each document
SELECT
    doc_id,
    COUNT(version_id) AS version_count
FROM
    Versions
GROUP BY
    doc_id
ORDER BY
    doc_id;

text_es: Schema: Threads (thread_id, title, user_id, created_at, status), Posts (post_id, thread_id, user_id, content, posted_at, is_deleted). Queries: 1. Get all posts for a specific thread, excluding deleted ones. 2. Find threads started by a particular user. 3. Update the status of a thread (e.g., 'closed', 'open'). 4. Soft-delete a specific post. 5. Count the number of posts per thread.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get all posts for a specific thread, excluding deleted ones.
SELECT
    post_id,
    thread_id,
    user_id,
    content,
    posted_at
FROM
    Posts
WHERE
    thread_id = 123
    AND is_deleted = FALSE;

-- 2. Find threads started by a particular user.
SELECT
    thread_id,
    title,
    created_at,
    status
FROM
    Threads
WHERE
    user_id = 456;

-- 3. Update the status of a thread (e.g., 'closed', 'open').
UPDATE
    Threads
SET
    status = 'closed'
WHERE
    thread_id = 789;

-- 4. Soft-delete a specific post.
UPDATE
    Posts
SET
    is_deleted = TRUE
WHERE
    post_id = 1011;

-- 5. Count the number of posts per thread.
SELECT
    t.thread_id,
    t.title,
    COUNT(p.post_id) AS post_count
FROM
    Threads AS t
LEFT JOIN
    Posts AS p ON t.thread_id = p.thread_id
GROUP BY
    t.thread_id, t.title
ORDER BY
    post_count DESC;

Queries: 1. Retrieve all questions for a given survey. 2. Get all responses for a specific question. 3. Insert a new response for a question from a participant. 4. Find the total number of responses for each survey. 5. List all participants who answered a specific survey.
text_nat:
-- 1. Retrieve all questions for a given survey (e.g., survey_id = 1)
SELECT
    question_id,
    question_text,
    question_type
FROM
    Questions
WHERE
    survey_id = 1;

-- 2. Get all responses for a specific question (e.g., question_id = 101)
SELECT
    response_id,
    participant_id,
    response_value,
    responded_at
FROM
    Responses
WHERE
    question_id = 101;

-- 3. Insert a new response for a question from a participant
INSERT INTO Responses (question_id, participant_id, response_value, responded_at)
VALUES (102, 501, 'Satisfied', NOW());

-- 4. Find the total number of responses for each survey
SELECT
    s.title,
    COUNT(r.response_id) AS total_responses
FROM
    Surveys AS s
JOIN
    Questions AS q ON s.survey_id = q.survey_id
LEFT JOIN
    Responses AS r ON q.question_id = r.question_id
GROUP BY
    s.title
ORDER BY
    total_responses DESC;

-- 5. List all participants who answered a specific survey (e.g., survey_id = 1)
SELECT DISTINCT
    r.participant_id
FROM
    Responses AS r
JOIN
    Questions AS q ON r.question_id = q.question_id
WHERE
    q.survey_id = 1;

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username, email), Subscriptions (sub_id, user_id, tier_id, start_date, end_date, is_active), Tiers (tier_id, tier_name, price_monthly). Queries: 1. Find the current active subscription tier for a user. 2. List all users on a specific subscription tier. 3. Update a user's subscription to a new tier (end current, start new). 4. Get the count of active users per tier. 5. Find all users whose subscriptions are expiring in the next 30 days.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Find the current active subscription tier for a user.
SELECT
    U.username,
    T.tier_name
FROM
    Users AS U
JOIN
    Subscriptions AS S ON U.user_id = S.user_id
JOIN
    Tiers AS T ON S.tier_id = T.tier_id
WHERE
    U.user_id = 123 AND S.is_active = TRUE AND S.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE;

-- Query 2: List all users on a specific subscription tier.
SELECT
    U.username,
    U.email
FROM
    Users AS U
JOIN
    Subscriptions AS S ON U.user_id = S.user_id
JOIN
    Tiers AS T ON S.tier_id = T.tier_id
WHERE
    T.tier_name = 'Premium' AND S.is_active = TRUE AND S.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE;

-- Query 3: Update a user's subscription to a new tier (end current, start new).
UPDATE Subscriptions
SET
    is_active = FALSE,
    end_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE
    user_id = 123 AND is_active = TRUE;

INSERT INTO Subscriptions (user_id, tier_id, start_date, end_date, is_active)
VALUES (123, 456, CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '1 year', TRUE);

-- Query 4: Get the count of active users per tier.
SELECT
    T.tier_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT S.user_id) AS active_user_count
FROM
    Subscriptions AS S
JOIN
    Tiers AS T ON S.tier_id = T.tier_id
WHERE
    S.is_active = TRUE AND S.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE
GROUP BY
    T.tier_name
ORDER BY
    active_user_count DESC;

-- Query 5: Find all users whose subscriptions are expiring in the next 30 days.
SELECT
    U.username,
    U.email,
    S.end_date
FROM
    Users AS U
JOIN
    Subscriptions AS S ON U.user_id = S.user_id
WHERE
    S.is_active = TRUE
    AND S.end_date >= CURRENT_DATE
    AND S.end_date <= CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '30 days';

text_es: Schema: Customers (customer_id, customer_name, email), Transactions (transaction_id, customer_id, amount, transaction_date), LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_balance, last_updated). Queries: 1. Get the current loyalty points for a customer. 2. Update a customer's loyalty points after a transaction (add points). 3. Find all customers with more than X points. 4. Get the total transaction amount for each customer. 5. List customers who haven't earned points in the last 90 days.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the current loyalty points for a customer
SELECT
    points_balance
FROM
    LoyaltyPoints
WHERE
    customer_id = 101;

-- 2. Update a customer's loyalty points after a transaction (add points).
-- Assuming 1 point per $10 spent
UPDATE LoyaltyPoints
SET
    points_balance = points_balance + (SELECT amount / 10 FROM Transactions WHERE transaction_id = 2001)
WHERE
    customer_id = (SELECT customer_id FROM Transactions WHERE transaction_id = 2001);

-- 3. Find all customers with more than X points
SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    lp.points_balance
FROM
    Customers AS c
JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp ON c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.points_balance > 500;

-- 4. Get the total transaction amount for each customer
SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    SUM(t.amount) AS total_spent
FROM
    Customers AS c
LEFT JOIN
    Transactions AS t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
GROUP BY
    c.customer_name
ORDER BY
    total_spent DESC;

-- 5. List customers who haven't earned points in the last 90 days
SELECT
    c.customer_name
FROM
    Customers AS c
LEFT JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp ON c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.last_updated IS NULL OR lp.last_updated < DATE('now', '-90 days');

    Sales AS S

    Salespeople AS SP ON S.salesperson_id = SP.salesperson_id
JOIN
    Regions AS R ON SP.region_id = R.region_id

    R.region_name = 'East';

    Salespeople AS SP ON S.salesperson_id = SP.salesperson_id

text_es: Schema: Recipes (recipe_id, recipe_name, instructions), Ingredients (ingredient_id, ingredient_name, unit_of_measure), RecipeIngredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id, quantity_needed), Inventory (ingredient_id, quantity_on_hand, last_restocked). Queries: 1. List all ingredients for a specific recipe, with quantities. 2. Find recipes that can be made with current inventory (assuming enough of all ingredients). 3. Update the quantity on hand for an ingredient in inventory. 4. Get a list of ingredients that are low in stock (e.g., quantity_on_hand < 10). 5. Find recipes that use a particular ingredient.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all ingredients for a specific recipe, with quantities.
SELECT
    R.recipe_name,
    I.ingredient_name,
    RI.quantity_needed,
    I.unit_of_measure
FROM
    Recipes AS R
JOIN
    RecipeIngredients AS RI ON R.recipe_id = RI.recipe_id
JOIN
    Ingredients AS I ON RI.ingredient_id = I.ingredient_id
WHERE
    R.recipe_name = 'Spaghetti Carbonara';

-- 2. Find recipes that can be made with current inventory.
SELECT
    R.recipe_name
FROM
    Recipes AS R
WHERE
    NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM RecipeIngredients AS RI
        JOIN Inventory AS INV ON RI.ingredient_id = INV.ingredient_id
        WHERE R.recipe_id = RI.recipe_id AND RI.quantity_needed > INV.quantity_on_hand
    );

-- 3. Update the quantity on hand for an ingredient in inventory.
UPDATE Inventory
SET quantity_on_hand = 75
WHERE ingredient_id = (SELECT ingredient_id FROM Ingredients WHERE ingredient_name = 'Flour');

-- 4. Get a list of ingredients that are low in stock.
SELECT
    I.ingredient_name,
    INV.quantity_on_hand,
    I.unit_of_measure
FROM
    Ingredients AS I
JOIN
    Inventory AS INV ON I.ingredient_id = INV.ingredient_id
WHERE
    INV.quantity_on_hand < 10
ORDER BY
    INV.quantity_on_hand;

-- 5. Find recipes that use a particular ingredient.
SELECT
    R.recipe_name
FROM
    Recipes AS R
JOIN
    RecipeIngredients AS RI ON R.recipe_id = RI.recipe_id
JOIN
    Ingredients AS I ON RI.ingredient_id = I.ingredient_id
WHERE
    I.ingredient_name = 'Garlic';

text_es: Schema: Vehicles (vehicle_id, make, model, year, license_plate), MaintenanceRecords (record_id, vehicle_id, service_type, service_date, cost, mileage_at_service). Queries: 1. Get all maintenance records for a specific vehicle. 2. Find the total maintenance cost for each vehicle. 3. Insert a new maintenance record. 4. Find vehicles that haven't had a specific service type in over a year. 5. List vehicles due for service based on mileage (e.g., last service at 50k, due every 10k, current mileage 59k).
text_nat:
-- 1. Get all maintenance records for a specific vehicle
SELECT *
FROM MaintenanceRecords
WHERE vehicle_id = 1;

-- 2. Find the total maintenance cost for each vehicle
SELECT v.make, v.model, SUM(mr.cost) AS total_cost
FROM Vehicles AS v
JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr
ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id, v.make, v.model;

-- 3. Insert a new maintenance record
INSERT INTO MaintenanceRecords (vehicle_id, service_type, service_date, cost, mileage_at_service)
VALUES (1, 'Oil Change', '2023-10-26', 75.00, 60500);

-- 4. Find vehicles that haven't had a specific service type in over a year
SELECT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate
FROM Vehicles AS v
WHERE v.vehicle_id NOT IN (
    SELECT mr.vehicle_id
    FROM MaintenanceRecords AS mr
    WHERE mr.service_type = 'Brake Replacement'
    AND mr.service_date >= DATE('now', '-1 year')
);

-- 5. List vehicles due for service based on mileage
-- (Assuming a service interval of 10000 miles and current mileage is known)
WITH LastService AS (
    SELECT
        vehicle_id,
        MAX(mileage_at_service) AS last_service_mileage,
        MAX(service_date) AS last_service_date
    FROM MaintenanceRecords
    GROUP BY vehicle_id
)
SELECT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate, ls.last_service_mileage
FROM Vehicles AS v
JOIN LastService AS ls
ON v.vehicle_id = ls.vehicle_id
WHERE (ls.last_service_mileage + 10000) <= (
    SELECT MAX(mileage_at_service)
    FROM MaintenanceRecords
    WHERE vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
);

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name), Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd). Queries: 1. Get the current price for a specific product. 2. List the full pricing history for a product. 3. Insert a new price for a product (new effective date). 4. Find products whose price has increased in the last year. 5. Get the latest price for all products.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the current price for a specific product
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    pr.price_usd
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Prices AS pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE
    p.product_id = 1
AND
    pr.effective_date = (
        SELECT MAX(effective_date)
        FROM Prices
        WHERE product_id = p.product_id
    );

-- 2. List the full pricing history for a product
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    pr.effective_date,
    pr.price_usd
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Prices AS pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE
    p.product_id = 1
ORDER BY
    pr.effective_date DESC;

-- 3. Insert a new price for a product (new effective date)
INSERT INTO Prices (product_id, effective_date, price_usd)
VALUES (1, '2023-11-01', 25.00);

-- 4. Find products whose price has increased in the last year
WITH RankedPrices AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        effective_date,
        price_usd,
        LAG(price_usd) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY effective_date) AS previous_price,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY effective_date DESC) AS rn
    FROM
        Prices
    WHERE
        effective_date >= DATE('now', '-1 year')
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.product_name
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    RankedPrices AS rp ON p.product_id = rp.product_id
WHERE
    rp.rn = 1 AND rp.price_usd > rp.previous_price;

-- 5. Get the latest price for all products
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    pr.price_usd
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Prices AS pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE
    pr.effective_date = (
        SELECT MAX(effective_date)
        FROM Prices
        WHERE product_id = p.product_id
    );

List all expenses for a department in a given month. 3. Insert a new expense record. 4. Find departments that are over budget. 5. Get the remaining budget for each department.

FROM Expenses

  d.dept_name,
  d.budget_total,
  SUM(e.amount) AS total_spent
FROM Departments AS d
JOIN Expenses AS e
  ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
GROUP BY
  d.dept_id,
  d.dept_name,

HAVING
  SUM(e.amount) > d.budget_total;

GROUP BY
  d.dept_id,

text_es: Schema: Agents (agent_id, agent_name, department), Tickets (ticket_id, agent_id, customer_id, opened_at, closed_at, status, resolution_notes). Queries: 1. Get the number of tickets closed by a specific agent. 2. List all open tickets assigned to an agent. 3. Assign a ticket to an agent. 4. Close a ticket with resolution notes. 5. Find agents with an average resolution time longer than X hours.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the number of tickets closed by a specific agent.
SELECT COUNT(ticket_id)
FROM Tickets
WHERE agent_id = 'agent_123' AND status = 'Closed';

-- 2. List all open tickets assigned to an agent.
SELECT ticket_id, customer_id, opened_at
FROM Tickets
WHERE agent_id = 'agent_456' AND status = 'Open';

-- 3. Assign a ticket to an agent.
UPDATE Tickets
SET agent_id = 'agent_789'
WHERE ticket_id = 'ticket_001' AND agent_id IS NULL;

-- 4. Close a ticket with resolution notes.
UPDATE Tickets
SET status = 'Closed', closed_at = NOW(), resolution_notes = 'Issue resolved successfully.'
WHERE ticket_id = 'ticket_002';

-- 5. Find agents with an average resolution time longer than X hours.
SELECT
    a.agent_name,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.closed_at - t.opened_at))) / 3600 AS avg_resolution_hours
FROM
    Agents AS a
JOIN
    Tickets AS t ON a.agent_id = t.agent_id
WHERE
    t.status = 'Closed'
GROUP BY
    a.agent_name
HAVING
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.closed_at - t.opened_at))) / 3600 > 8; -- X hours = 8

text_es: Schema: Projects (project_id, project_name, start_date, end_date), Tasks (task_id, project_id, task_name, due_date, status), TaskDependencies (task_id, depends_on_task_id). Queries: 1. FROM TaskDependencies TD JOIN Tasks T1 ON TD.task_id = T1.task_id
JOIN Tasks T2 ON TD.depends_on_task_id = T2.task_id
WHERE T1.task_id = 101;

FROM Tasks T
LEFT JOIN TaskDependencies TD ON T.task_id = TD.task_id
LEFT JOIN Tasks DependentTask ON TD.depends_on_task_id = DependentTask.task_id
WHERE T.status = 'pending'
GROUP BY T.task_id, T.task_name
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN DependentTask.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) = COUNT(TD.depends_on_task_id);

SELECT T.task_id, T.task_name, COUNT(TD.depends_on_task_id) AS dependency_count
FROM Tasks T
LEFT JOIN TaskDependencies TD ON T.task_id = TD.task_id
GROUP BY T.task_id, T.task_name
ORDER BY dependency_count DESC;

    L.location_name
FROM

FROM
    Assets AS A
JOIN
    AssetLocations AS AL ON A.asset_id = AL.asset_id
JOIN
    Locations AS L ON AL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE
    L.location_name = 'Data Center A'
    AND AL.released_date IS NULL;

-- Query 3: Assign an asset to a new location (end old assignment, start new)
UPDATE AssetLocations
SET released_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE asset_id = 456 AND released_date IS NULL;

INSERT INTO AssetLocations (asset_id, location_id, assigned_date, released_date)
VALUES (456, 101, CURRENT_DATE, NULL);

-- Query 4: Find assets purchased before a specific date
SELECT
    asset_tag,
    purchase_date,
    cost
FROM
    Assets
WHERE
    purchase_date < '2022-01-01';

-- Query 5: Get the total cost of assets per asset type
SELECT
    asset_type,
    SUM(cost) AS total_cost
FROM
    Assets
GROUP BY
    asset_type
ORDER BY
    total_cost DESC;

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name, price), Customers (customer_id, customer_name), Returns (return_id, customer_id, product_id, return_date, reason, refund_amount). Queries: 1. List all returns made by a specific customer. 2. Find all returns for a particular product. 3. Insert a new product return record. 4. Get the total refund amount for each customer. 5. Find products with more than 10 returns in the last month.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all returns made by a specific customer
SELECT *
FROM Returns
WHERE customer_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all returns for a particular product
SELECT *
FROM Returns
WHERE product_id = 101;

-- 3. Insert a new product return record
INSERT INTO Returns (return_id, customer_id, product_id, return_date, reason, refund_amount)
VALUES (1001, 5, 105, '2023-10-26', 'Defective', 59.99);

-- 4. Get the total refund amount for each customer
SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    SUM(r.refund_amount) AS total_refund_amount
FROM Customers AS c
JOIN Returns AS r
ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_name;

-- 5. Find products with more than 10 returns in the last month
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    COUNT(r.return_id) AS total_returns
FROM Products AS p
JOIN Returns AS r
ON p.product_id = r.product_id
WHERE r.return_date >= DATE('now', '-1 month')
GROUP BY p.product_name
HAVING COUNT(r.return_id) > 10
ORDER BY total_returns DESC;

text_es: Schema: Employees (employee_id, employee_name, manager_id), Reviews (review_id, employee_id, reviewer_id, review_date, overall_rating, comments). Queries: 1. List all reviews for a specific employee. 2. Find all employees reviewed by a particular manager. 3. Insert a new performance review. 4. Get the average rating for each employee. 5. List employees who have not had a review in the last year.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all reviews for a specific employee (e.g., employee_id = 1)
SELECT
    R.review_id,
    R.reviewer_id,
    R.review_date,
    R.overall_rating,
    R.comments
FROM
    Reviews AS R
WHERE
    R.employee_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all employees reviewed by a particular manager (e.g., manager_id = 2)
SELECT DISTINCT
    E.employee_id,
    E.employee_name
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    Reviews AS R ON E.employee_id = R.employee_id
WHERE
    R.reviewer_id = 2;

-- 3. Insert a new performance review
INSERT INTO Reviews (employee_id, reviewer_id, review_date, overall_rating, comments)
VALUES (3, 1, '2023-10-26', 4, 'Excellent performance this quarter.');

-- 4. Get the average rating for each employee
SELECT
    E.employee_name,
    AVG(R.overall_rating) AS average_rating
FROM
    Employees AS E
LEFT JOIN
    Reviews AS R ON E.employee_id = R.employee_id
GROUP BY
    E.employee_name
ORDER BY
    E.employee_name;

-- 5. List employees who have not had a review in the last year
SELECT
    E.employee_id,
    E.employee_name
FROM
    Employees AS E
LEFT JOIN
    Reviews AS R ON E.employee_id = R.employee_id
GROUP BY
    E.employee_id, E.employee_name
HAVING
    MAX(R.review_date) IS NULL OR MAX(R.review_date) < DATE('now', '-1 year');

text_es: Schema: Subscriptions (sub_id, user_id, plan_id, start_date, end_date), Plans (plan_id, plan_name, monthly_cost, data_limit_gb), UsageRecords (usage_id, sub_id, usage_date, data_used_gb). Queries: 1. Get the total data used by a specific subscription in a month. 2. List all subscriptions on a particular plan. 3. Record new data usage for a subscription. 4. Find subscriptions that have exceeded their data limit. 5. Calculate the remaining data limit for each active subscription.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the total data used by a specific subscription in a month.
SELECT
    SUM(data_used_gb) AS total_data_used
FROM
    UsageRecords
WHERE
    sub_id = 101 AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', usage_date) = '2023-10';

-- 2. List all subscriptions on a particular plan.
SELECT
    s.sub_id,
    s.user_id,
    s.start_date,
    s.end_date
FROM
    Subscriptions AS s
JOIN
    Plans AS p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
WHERE
    p.plan_name = 'Premium Plan';

-- 3. Record new data usage for a subscription.
INSERT INTO UsageRecords (sub_id, usage_date, data_used_gb)
VALUES (101, '2023-11-15', 5.2);

-- 4. Find subscriptions that have exceeded their data limit.
SELECT
    s.sub_id,
    s.user_id,
    p.plan_name,
    p.data_limit_gb,
    SUM(ur.data_used_gb) AS total_data_used_current_month
FROM
    Subscriptions AS s
JOIN
    Plans AS p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
JOIN
    UsageRecords AS ur ON s.sub_id = ur.sub_id
WHERE
    STRFTIME('%Y-%m', ur.usage_date) = STRFTIME('%Y-%m', 'now')
GROUP BY
    s.sub_id, s.user_id, p.plan_name, p.data_limit_gb
HAVING
    SUM(ur.data_used_gb) > p.data_limit_gb;

-- 5. Calculate the remaining data limit for each active subscription.
SELECT
    s.sub_id,
    s.user_id,
    p.plan_name,
    p.data_limit_gb - COALESCE(SUM(ur.data_used_gb), 0) AS remaining_data_gb
FROM
    Subscriptions AS s
JOIN
    Plans AS p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
LEFT JOIN
    UsageRecords AS ur ON s.sub_id = ur.sub_id
    AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', ur.usage_date) = STRFTIME('%Y-%m', 'now')
WHERE
    DATE('now') BETWEEN s.start_date AND s.end_date
GROUP BY
    s.sub_id, s.user_id, p.plan_name, p.data_limit_gb
ORDER BY
    s.sub_id;

text_es: Schema: Employees (employee_id, employee_name, manager_id), TimeOffTypes (type_id, type_name), TimeOffRequests (request_id, employee_id, type_id, start_date, end_date, status, approved_by_manager_id). Queries: 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee. 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager. 3. Submit a new time off request. 4. Approve a time off request. 5. Get the total number of days requested per time off type.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee.
SELECT
    request_id,
    employee_id,
    type_id,
    start_date,
    end_date
FROM
    TimeOffRequests
WHERE
    employee_id = 101 AND status = 'Pending';

-- 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager.
SELECT
    tor.request_id,
    e.employee_name AS employee,
    tot.type_name AS time_off_type,
    tor.start_date,
    tor.end_date
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS tor
JOIN
    Employees AS e ON tor.employee_id = e.employee_id
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS tot ON tor.type_id = tot.type_id
WHERE
    tor.status = 'Pending' AND e.manager_id = 201;

-- 3. Submit a new time off request.
INSERT INTO TimeOffRequests (employee_id, type_id, start_date, end_date, status)
VALUES (105, 3, '2023-12-25', '2023-12-26', 'Pending');

-- 4. Approve a time off request.
UPDATE TimeOffRequests
SET
    status = 'Approved',
    approved_by_manager_id = 201
WHERE
    request_id = 501 AND status = 'Pending';

-- 5. Get the total number of days requested per time off type.
SELECT
    tot.type_name,
    SUM(JULIANDAY(tor.end_date) - JULIANDAY(tor.start_date) + 1) AS total_days_requested
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS tor
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS tot ON tor.type_id = tot.type_id
GROUP BY
    tot.type_name
ORDER BY
    total_days_requested DESC;

text_es: Schema: MenuItems (item_id, item_name, description, price), Days (day_id, day_name), DailyMenu (daily_menu_id, day_id, item_id). Queries: 1. List all menu items for a specific day. 2. text_nat:

    Days AS d ON dm.day_id = d.day_id

FROM

JOIN
    DailyMenu AS dm ON d.day_id = dm.day_id
JOIN
    MenuItems AS mi ON dm.item_id = mi.item_id
WHERE
    mi.item_name = 'Spaghetti Carbonara';

WHERE

-- 5. Get the count of times each menu item appears on the menu
SELECT
    mi.item_name,
    COUNT(dm.item_id) AS appearance_count
FROM
    MenuItems AS mi
LEFT JOIN
    DailyMenu AS dm ON mi.item_id = dm.item_id
GROUP BY
    mi.item_name
ORDER BY
    appearance_count DESC;

text_es: Schema: Events (event_id, event_name, event_date, ticket_price), Tickets (ticket_id, event_id, customer_id, purchase_date, quantity). Queries: 1. Get the total revenue for a specific event. 2. List all tickets purchased by a specific customer. 3. Record new ticket sales for an event. 4. Find events that are sold out (assuming a fixed capacity, not in schema). 5. Get the total number of tickets sold per event.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the total revenue for a specific event
SELECT
    SUM(T.quantity * E.ticket_price) AS total_revenue
FROM
    Tickets AS T
JOIN
    Events AS E ON T.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE
    E.event_name = 'Concert in the Park';

-- 2. List all tickets purchased by a specific customer
SELECT
    T.ticket_id,
    E.event_name,
    T.purchase_date,
    T.quantity
FROM
    Tickets AS T
JOIN
    Events AS E ON T.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE
    T.customer_id = 101;

-- 3. Record new ticket sales for an event
INSERT INTO Tickets (event_id, customer_id, purchase_date, quantity)
VALUES (1, 102, '2023-10-26', 2);

-- 4. Find events that are sold out (assuming a fixed capacity of 100 for all events)
SELECT
    E.event_name
FROM
    Events AS E
JOIN
    (SELECT event_id, SUM(quantity) AS total_sold FROM Tickets GROUP BY event_id) AS TS
ON
    E.event_id = TS.event_id
WHERE
    TS.total_sold >= 100; -- Assuming a fixed capacity of 100

-- 5. Get the total number of tickets sold per event
SELECT
    E.event_name,
    SUM(T.quantity) AS total_tickets_sold
FROM
    Events AS E
LEFT JOIN
    Tickets AS T ON E.event_id = T.event_id
GROUP BY
    E.event_name
ORDER BY
    total_tickets_sold DESC;

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name, base_price), Variants (variant_id, product_id, color, size, sku, stock_quantity, additional_cost). Queries: 1. List all variants for a specific product. 2. Find all products that have a variant with a specific color. 3. Update the stock quantity for a variant. 4. Get the full price (base_price + additional_cost) for each variant. 5. Find products with no variants currently in stock.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all variants for a specific product
SELECT *
FROM Variants
WHERE product_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all products that have a variant with a specific color
SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name
FROM Products AS p
JOIN Variants AS v
ON p.product_id = v.product_id
WHERE v.color = 'Red';

-- 3. Update the stock quantity for a variant
UPDATE Variants
SET stock_quantity = 50
WHERE variant_id = 101;

-- 4. Get the full price (base_price + additional_cost) for each variant
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    v.color,
    v.size,
    (p.base_price + v.additional_cost) AS full_price
FROM Products AS p
JOIN Variants AS v
ON p.product_id = v.product_id;

-- 5. Find products with no variants currently in stock
SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products AS p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM Variants AS v
    WHERE v.product_id = p.product_id AND v.stock_quantity > 0
);

GROUP BY

FROM

JOIN
  PostTags AS pt ON p.post_id = pt.post_id
JOIN
  Tags AS t ON pt.tag_id = t.tag_id
WHERE
  t.tag_name = 'SQL';

-- 2. List all tags for a particular post (e.g., post_id = 1)
SELECT
  t.tag_name
FROM
  Tags AS t
JOIN
  PostTags AS pt ON t.tag_id = pt.tag_id
WHERE
  pt.post_id = 1;

-- 3. Add a tag (e.g., 'Database') to a post (e.g., post_id = 2)
INSERT INTO PostTags (post_id, tag_id)
SELECT
  2, t.tag_id
FROM
  Tags AS t
WHERE
  t.tag_name = 'Database';

-- 4. Remove a tag (e.g., 'SQL') from a post (e.g., post_id = 1)
DELETE FROM PostTags
WHERE
  post_id = 1

-- 5. Get the count of posts for each tag
SELECT
  t.tag_name,
  COUNT(pt.post_id) AS post_count
FROM
  Tags AS t
LEFT JOIN
  PostTags AS pt ON t.tag_id = pt.tag_id
GROUP BY
  t.tag_name
ORDER BY

    U.username,
    MP.plan_date,
    MP.meal_type
FROM
    MealPlans MP
JOIN

JOIN

JOIN

3. Add a new book to the inventory.
4. Update the price of a book.
5. Calculate the total sales for each genre.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all books by a specific author.
SELECT book_id, title, author, genre, price, stock_quantity
FROM Books
WHERE author = 'Jane Austen';

-- 2. List all orders made by a particular customer.
SELECT O.order_id, O.order_date, O.total_amount
FROM Orders AS O
JOIN Customers AS C ON O.customer_id = C.customer_id
WHERE C.name = 'Alice Smith';

-- 3. Add a new book to the inventory.
INSERT INTO Books (book_id, title, author, genre, price, stock_quantity)
VALUES (101, 'The Great Adventure', 'John Doe', 'Adventure', 15.99, 50);

-- 4. Update the price of a book.
UPDATE Books
SET price = 22.50
WHERE title = 'Pride and Prejudice';

-- 5. Calculate the total sales for each genre.
SELECT B.genre, SUM(O.total_amount) AS total_sales_by_genre
FROM Orders AS O
JOIN Books AS B ON O.order_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT order_id FROM OrderItems WHERE book_id = B.book_id) -- Assuming an OrderItems table for actual book sales
GROUP BY B.genre
ORDER BY total_sales_by_genre DESC;

Queries:

2. Find the total revenue generated by each event.
3. Register a new attendee for an event.
4. Update an event's location.
5. List events with more than 50 tickets sold.
text_nat:
-- 1. Select all attendees for a specific event
SELECT
    A.name AS attendee_name,
    A.email
FROM
    Attendees AS A
JOIN
    Tickets AS T ON A.attendee_id = T.attendee_id
JOIN
    Events AS E ON T.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE
    E.name = 'Conference 2023';

-- 2. Find the total revenue generated by each event
SELECT
    E.name AS event_name,
    SUM(T.price_paid) AS total_revenue
FROM
    Events AS E
JOIN
    Tickets AS T ON E.event_id = T.event_id
GROUP BY
    E.name;

SET
    location = 'New Convention Center'
WHERE

    COUNT(T.ticket_id) AS tickets_sold
FROM
    Events AS E
JOIN
    Tickets AS T ON E.event_id = T.event_id
GROUP BY
    E.name
HAVING
    COUNT(T.ticket_id) > 50;

Queries:
1. Find all available rooms for a given date range.
2. List all bookings made by a specific guest.
3. Create a new room booking.
4. Update a room's status to 'occupied'.
5. Calculate the total revenue from bookings per room type.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all available rooms for a given date range
SELECT
    r.room_id,
    r.room_number,
    r.type,
    r.price_per_night
FROM
    Rooms AS r
WHERE
    r.status = 'available'
    AND r.room_id NOT IN (
        SELECT
            b.room_id
        FROM
            Bookings AS b
        WHERE
            (b.check_in_date <= '2023-10-20' AND b.check_out_date >= '2023-10-15')
    );

-- 2. List all bookings made by a specific guest
SELECT
    b.booking_id,
    r.room_number,
    b.check_in_date,
    b.check_out_date,
    b.total_price
FROM
    Bookings AS b
JOIN
    Rooms AS r ON b.room_id = r.room_id
WHERE
    b.guest_id = 1; -- Assuming guest_id = 1 for a specific guest

-- 3. Create a new room booking
INSERT INTO Bookings (room_id, guest_id, check_in_date, check_out_date, total_price)
VALUES (101, 5, '2023-11-01', '2023-11-05', 400.00);

-- 4. Update a room's status to 'occupied'
UPDATE
    Rooms
SET
    status = 'occupied'
WHERE
    room_id = 101;

-- 5. Calculate the total revenue from bookings per room type
SELECT
    r.type,
    SUM(b.total_price) AS total_revenue
FROM
    Bookings AS b
JOIN
    Rooms AS r ON b.room_id = r.room_id
GROUP BY
    r.type
ORDER BY
    total_revenue DESC;

Schema: Items (item_id INT, name VARCHAR, weight DECIMAL, dimensions VARCHAR), Locations (location_id INT, warehouse_name VARCHAR, aisle VARCHAR, rack VARCHAR), ItemLocations (item_id INT, location_id INT, quantity INT, last_moved DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse.
2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
3. Add new stock of an item to a location.
4. Move an item from one location to another.
5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse.
SELECT
    I.name,
    I.item_id
FROM
    Items AS I
JOIN
    ItemLocations AS IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
JOIN
    Locations AS L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE
    L.warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND L.aisle = 'A1';

-- 2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
SELECT
    L.warehouse_name,
    L.aisle,
    L.rack,
    IL.quantity
FROM
    Locations AS L
JOIN
    ItemLocations AS IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id
JOIN
    Items AS I ON IL.item_id = I.item_id
WHERE
    I.name = 'Laptop Charger';

-- 3. Add new stock of an item to a location.
INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved)
VALUES
    (101, 1, 50, '2023-10-26 10:00:00')
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
    quantity = quantity + VALUES(quantity), last_moved = VALUES(last_moved);

-- 4. Move an item from one location to another.
-- This involves updating quantities in two locations.
-- Assuming item_id = 101, old_location_id = 1, new_location_id = 2, quantity_to_move = 10
UPDATE ItemLocations
SET quantity = quantity - 10, last_moved = NOW()
WHERE item_id = 101 AND location_id = 1;

UPDATE ItemLocations
SET quantity = quantity + 10, last_moved = NOW()
WHERE item_id = 101 AND location_id = 2;

-- 5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
SELECT
    I.name,
    SUM(IL.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM
    Items AS I
JOIN
    ItemLocations AS IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
GROUP BY
    I.name
ORDER BY
    total_quantity DESC;

Schema: Teams (team_id INT, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR), Matches (match_id INT, home_team_id INT, away_team_id INT, match_date DATETIME, home_score INT, away_score INT), Players (player_id INT, team_id INT, name VARCHAR, position VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all matches played by a specific team.
2. List all players on a particular team.
3. Record a new match score.
4. Update a player's position.
5. Calculate the total wins for each team.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all matches played by a specific team.
SELECT
    M.match_id,
    T_HOME.name AS home_team_name,
    T_AWAY.name AS away_team_name,
    M.match_date,
    M.home_score,
    M.away_score
FROM
    Matches M
JOIN
    Teams T_HOME ON M.home_team_id = T_HOME.team_id
JOIN
    Teams T_AWAY ON M.away_team_id = T_AWAY.team_id
WHERE
    T_HOME.name = 'Team A' OR T_AWAY.name = 'Team A';

-- 2. List all players on a particular team.
SELECT
    P.name AS player_name,
    P.position
FROM
    Players P
JOIN
    Teams T ON P.team_id = T.team_id
WHERE
    T.name = 'Team B';

-- 3. Record a new match score.
UPDATE Matches
SET
    home_score = 3,
    away_score = 1
WHERE
    match_id = 101;

-- 4. Update a player's position.
UPDATE Players
SET
    position = 'Midfielder'
WHERE
    player_id = 205;

-- 5. Calculate the total wins for each team.
SELECT
    T.name AS team_name,
    COUNT(CASE
        WHEN M.home_team_id = T.team_id AND M.home_score > M.away_score THEN 1
        WHEN M.away_team_id = T.team_id AND M.away_score > M.home_score THEN 1
        ELSE NULL
    END) AS total_wins
FROM
    Teams T
LEFT JOIN
    Matches M ON T.team_id = M.home_team_id OR T.team_id = M.away_team_id
GROUP BY
    T.team_id, T.name
ORDER BY
    total_wins DESC;
