Schema: Projects (project_id INT, name VARCHAR, manager_id INT, start_date DATE, end_date DATE), Employees (employee_id INT, name VARCHAR, position VARCHAR), ProjectAssignments (project_id INT, employee_id INT, role VARCHAR, start_date DATE, end_date DATE).
Queries:
1. Find all employees assigned to a specific project.
2. List all projects managed by a particular employee.
3. Assign an employee to a project.
4. Update an employee's role on a project.
5. Count the number of employees per project.
text_nat:
SELECT
    E.name AS EmployeeName,
    E.position
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
WHERE
    PA.project_id = 1;

SELECT
    P.name AS ProjectName,
    P.start_date,
    P.end_date
FROM
    Projects AS P
WHERE
    P.manager_id = 101;

INSERT INTO ProjectAssignments (project_id, employee_id, role, start_date, end_date)
VALUES (2, 203, 'Developer', '2023-10-01', '2024-03-31');

UPDATE ProjectAssignments
SET role = 'Senior Developer'
WHERE project_id = 1 AND employee_id = 201;

SELECT
    P.name AS ProjectName,
    COUNT(PA.employee_id) AS NumberOfEmployees
FROM
    Projects AS P
JOIN
    ProjectAssignments AS PA ON P.project_id = PA.project_id
GROUP BY
    P.name
ORDER BY
    NumberOfEmployees DESC;

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, registration_date DATETIME, last_login DATETIME), Pages (page_id INT, url VARCHAR, title VARCHAR), PageViews (view_id INT, user_id INT, page_id INT, view_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all pages viewed by a specific user.
2. List the top 5 most viewed pages.
3. Record a new page view.
4. Update a user's last login date.
5. Count the total page views for each user.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all pages viewed by a specific user (e.g., user_id = 1)
SELECT DISTINCT
    P.url,
    P.title
FROM
    Pages AS P
JOIN
    PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE
    PV.user_id = 1;

-- 2. List the top 5 most viewed pages
SELECT
    P.title,
    COUNT(PV.page_id) AS view_count
FROM
    Pages AS P
JOIN
    PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY
    P.page_id, P.title
ORDER BY
    view_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- 3. Record a new page view (e.g., user 2 viewing page 3 today)
INSERT INTO PageViews (user_id, page_id, view_date)
VALUES (2, 3, NOW());

-- 4. Update a user's last login date (e.g., for user_id = 1)
UPDATE Users
SET last_login = NOW()
WHERE user_id = 1;

-- 5. Count the total page views for each user
SELECT
    U.username,
    COUNT(PV.view_id) AS total_views
FROM
    Users AS U
LEFT JOIN
    PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY
    U.user_id, U.username
ORDER BY
    total_views DESC;
text_alt:
-- 1. Find all pages viewed by a specific user (e.g., user_id = 1)
select distinct

    P.title
from
    Pages as P
join

where
    PV.user_id = 1;

-- 2. List the top 5 most viewed pages
select
    P.title,
    count(PV.page_id) as view_count
from
    Pages as P
join
    PageViews as PV on P.page_id = PV.page_id
group by
    P.page_id, P.title
order by
    view_count desc
limit 5;

-- 3. Record a new page view (e.g., user 2 viewing page 3 today)
insert into PageViews (user_id, page_id, view_date)
values (2, 3, now());

-- 4. Update a user's last login date (e.g., for user_id = 1)
update Users
set last_login = now()
where user_id = 1;

-- 5. Count the total page views for each user
select
    U.username,
    count(PV.view_id) as total_views
from
    Users as U
left join
    PageViews as PV on U.user_id = PV.user_id
group by
    U.user_id, U.username
order by
    total_views desc;

Schema: Equipment (equipment_id INT, name VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, purchase_date DATE, status VARCHAR, department_id INT), Departments (department_id INT, name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR), Maintenance (maintenance_id INT, equipment_id INT, maintenance_date DATE, description TEXT, cost DECIMAL).
Queries:
1. Find all equipment in a specific department needing maintenance.
2. List all maintenance records for a particular piece of equipment.
3. Add a new piece of equipment.
4. Update an equipment's status to 'in repair'.
5. Calculate the total maintenance cost per equipment type.
text_nat:
SELECT E.equipment_id, E.name AS equipment_name, E.type, E.purchase_date, E.status
FROM Equipment AS E
JOIN Departments AS D ON E.department_id = D.department_id
WHERE D.name = 'Engineering' AND E.status = 'needs maintenance';

SELECT M.maintenance_id, M.maintenance_date, M.description, M.cost
FROM Maintenance AS M
WHERE M.equipment_id = 101;

INSERT INTO Equipment (equipment_id, name, type, purchase_date, status, department_id)
VALUES (201, 'Laser Printer', 'Printer', '2023-01-15', 'operational', 10);

UPDATE Equipment
SET status = 'in repair'
WHERE equipment_id = 102;

SELECT E.type, SUM(M.cost) AS total_maintenance_cost
FROM Equipment AS E
JOIN Maintenance AS M ON E.equipment_id = M.equipment_id
GROUP BY E.type
ORDER BY total_maintenance_cost DESC;

from Equipment as E

Schema: Students (student_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, class_id INT), Classes (class_id INT, name VARCHAR, teacher_id INT), Attendance (attendance_id INT, student_id INT, class_id INT, attendance_date DATE, status VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all attendance records for a specific student.
2. List all students marked 'Absent' for a particular class on a given date.
3. Record a student's attendance for a class.
4. Update an attendance record's status.
5. Count the total 'Present' records for each class.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all attendance records for a specific student.
SELECT
    attendance_id,
    attendance_date,
    status,
    C.name AS class_name
FROM
    Attendance A
JOIN
    Classes C ON A.class_id = C.class_id
WHERE
    student_id = 1;

-- 2. List all students marked 'Absent' for a particular class on a given date.
SELECT
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name
FROM
    Students S
JOIN
    Attendance A ON S.student_id = A.student_id
WHERE
    A.class_id = 101 AND A.attendance_date = '2023-10-26' AND A.status = 'Absent';

-- 3. Record a student's attendance for a class.
INSERT INTO Attendance (student_id, class_id, attendance_date, status)
VALUES (2, 102, '2023-10-27', 'Present');

-- 4. Update an attendance record's status.
UPDATE Attendance
SET status = 'Excused'
WHERE attendance_id = 5;

-- 5. Count the total 'Present' records for each class.
SELECT
    C.name AS class_name,
    COUNT(A.attendance_id) AS present_count
FROM
    Classes C
LEFT JOIN
    Attendance A ON C.class_id = A.class_id AND A.status = 'Present'
GROUP BY
    C.name
ORDER BY
    present_count DESC;

Schema: Employees (employee_id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR), Courses (course_id INT, title VARCHAR, duration_hours INT), TrainingRecords (record_id INT, employee_id INT, course_id INT, completion_date DATE, score INT).
Queries:
1. Find all training courses completed by a specific employee.
2. List all employees who completed a particular course with a score above 80.
3. Record a new training completion for an employee.
4. Update an employee's score for a completed course.
5. Calculate the average score for each course.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Find all training courses completed by a specific employee (e.g., employee_id = 1)
SELECT
    C.title,
    C.duration_hours,
    TR.completion_date,
    TR.score
FROM
    Courses AS C
JOIN
    TrainingRecords AS TR ON C.course_id = TR.course_id
WHERE
    TR.employee_id = 1;

-- Query 2: List all employees who completed a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101) with a score above 80
SELECT
    E.name,
    E.department,
    TR.score
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    TrainingRecords AS TR ON E.employee_id = TR.employee_id
WHERE
    TR.course_id = 101 AND TR.score > 80;

-- Query 3: Record a new training completion for an employee (e.g., employee_id = 2, course_id = 102, completion_date = '2023-10-26', score = 95)
INSERT INTO TrainingRecords (employee_id, course_id, completion_date, score)
VALUES (2, 102, '2023-10-26', 95);

-- Query 4: Update an employee's score for a completed course (e.g., employee_id = 1, course_id = 101, new score = 88)
UPDATE TrainingRecords
SET
    score = 88
WHERE
    employee_id = 1 AND course_id = 101;

-- Query 5: Calculate the average score for each course
SELECT
    C.title,
    AVG(TR.score) AS average_score
FROM
    Courses AS C
JOIN
    TrainingRecords AS TR ON C.course_id = TR.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.title
ORDER BY
    average_score DESC;
